jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Enterprise
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

Overview

Deepgram's next phase of growth is upmarket. Our customers have increasing compliance needs and are security-conscious buyers with sophisticated procurement orgs.

This role owns that problem space: making Deepgram enterprise-ready and removing the product blockers that stall upmarket deals. Enterprise buyers don't evaluate readiness as a feature. They evaluate it as a package — identity, security, compliance, and the experience their teams touch — and the absence of any one piece stalls a deal in security review. You own the outcome and ship the fix wherever it belongs: in Console, in our APIs, or in the managed endpoint, partnering with the PMs who own those surfaces.

Today that means enterprise SSO, FedRAMP/FIPS readiness, SBOM and security-artifact self-serve, and a user experience that signals maturity. The specifics will shift as we move upmarket; the mandate won't. This is high-leverage work with real autonomy. You set enterprise product strategy for a Series C company's core upmarket motion while owning a pillar of the business's strategy, with an explicit path to Staff as your scope grows.

What You'll Do

  • Own the enterprise adoption problem space end to end: the procurement, security, compliance, and UX storylines that have to work together to win upmarket deals.

  • Set strategy, sequencing across enterprise initiatives which today includes SSO, compliance readiness, and our Console UX, and defend that prioritization with data.

  • Ship solutions on whatever surface fits the problem: Console, APIs, or the managed endpoint. You own the problem and partner with the PMs who own those surfaces rather than owning the surfaces outright.

  • Drive enterprise security and compliance readiness so procurement teams can self-serve e.g., SBOM generation and security-artifact access, instead of waiting on us.

  • Remove the product blockers that stall deals in security review and slow closure.

  • Work directly with engineers, designers, and sales to ship features. Pull people in when you need to; don't wait for consensus.

  • Set your own objectives and make the trade-offs, with minimal steering.

You'll Love This Role If You

  • Want to own a pillar of company strategy rather than take tickets, and want the autonomy to set direction.

  • Get genuinely excited by enterprise complexity at scale such as turning identity, provisioning, RBAC, and audit into a package a security team will actually approve.

  • Care how a product feels, not just whether it works.

  • Can take a goal like "frictionless enterprise procurement" and derive a 12-week plan without asking "what should I do first?"

  • Are comfortable when requirements are imperfect and priorities shift.

  • Work AI-first by default and want to be on a team that does the same.

It's Important to Us That You Have

  • Enterprise product experience: you've shipped products into regulated or security-conscious customers and understand their procurement psychology.

  • Front-end/UX product sensibility: you bring the same rigor to how a product feels that enterprise teams bring to infrastructure.

  • Strong opinions backed by facts: you can defend your prioritization call with customer data, competitive positioning, and technical reality, and you update when new facts arrive.

  • An AI-native working style: AI is already part of how you research, analyze, prototype, and decide. This is about using AI to accelerate your own work, not outsourcing your judgment to an LLM. Expect us to probe it directly, including live.

  • Autonomous decision making and comfort with ambiguity: you thrive with objectives and minimal directional guidance.

  • Cross-functional range: you work fluently with engineers, designers, and sales.

It Would Be Great If You Had

  • A Computer Science / Software Engineering background: you understand how software works, why implementation has tradeoffs, and what Engineering needs to build a product.

  • Security or compliance shipping experience: FIPS, FedRAMP, SOC 2, or similar enterprise features.

  • Web console or platform-tooling experience: you know how to design experiences for technical audiences.

  • B2B or enterprise sales-cycle familiarity: you know what procurement orgs care about and why.

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Agentic Experiences (Former Engineer)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity

The way developers find and adopt an API is changing. More and more, an AI coding agent discovers us, chooses the provider, writes the integration, and consumes our API, often with no human ever at the console. Deepgram is looking for a Staff Product Manager to own our product experience for that agent across its whole life with us: how an agent discovers and chooses Deepgram, how it integrates, how it uses the product in production, and how it verifies its own work. You will own that experience end to end, and you will build the system that keeps improving it as agent behavior changes. You report to the VP of Self-Serve.

This is a product management role in the conventional sense: you own the product, its direction, and its decisions, and engineering builds it. Two things set the role apart, and both are required — you are a former engineer who still builds to think and to prove a point, and you are deeply AI-native, with shipped work to show for it. You will prototype, read and write code, and reason with engineering at depth; your job is to own the product, not to be its implementing engineer.

What You'll Do

- Own the agent's experience of Deepgram across its lifecycle — discovery and recommendation, integration and onboarding, production use, and verification.

- Stand up a system that measures and optimizes every stage of the funnel for agents, and keep it current as agent behavior changes.

- Own the product surfaces specific to the agent experience: signup and authentication, the trial-key and token defaults and programmatic key provisioning, console onboarding, and the verification tooling that lets an agent confirm its integration is actually correct.

- Set the requirements for what the agent experience needs from the shared developer platforms — SDK ergonomics, the agent-readable documentation and llms.txt, the MCP server, the CLI, the skills package, and starter templates — and prototype the changes directly, in partnership with the team that owns those platforms.

- Stand up the operating system your work runs on — the rhythms of business, data-driven optimization, and the experimentation platform — by building it in-house or by researching and deploying the best tools available.

- Turn the scale of agent traffic into fast feedback loops, so the product improves as agents use it.

- Bring the product's point of view on agents as users: what they need, where they fail, and what to change, grounded in how models actually retrieve, choose, and integrate.

You'll Love This Role If You

- Were an engineer, moved to product to own outcomes, and never stopped building.

- Think like an architect and can design and stand up a self-optimizing system across discovery, onboarding, and integration.

- Have felt, first-hand, how an AI agent succeeds or fails at a real integration, and have strong opinions about why.

- Want to own a product that is becoming the front door of the business, at the moment it is becoming that.

- Are energized by being early — defining the practice, not inheriting it.

It's Important to Us That You Have

- Excellent product management judgment. You own product and roadmap, set direction, decide under uncertainty, ship outcomes, and lead cross-functional work without authority. You can show the results.

- A former engineer's depth (required). You were a senior software engineer, or more, before you moved to product. You architect and ship production systems, you read and write real code, and you reason with engineering at their level. You are not a vibe coder who assembles what a tool generates.

- Deep AI fluency, proven by shipped work (required). You have personally built and shipped AI software that goes well beyond prompt files and markdown — agents, MCP servers, CLI tools, agent and evaluation harnesses, real model-integrated tools — and it is public. Send us the GitHub; we will read the code, the commits, and the design.

- Proven ability to stand up a complete system from scratch — the rhythms of business, the reporting and optimization, the experimentation platform — yourself or in-house, or by researching and deploying the right tools.

- PLG and developer-product fluency. You understand how developers, and increasingly their agents, adopt APIs, and you understand product-led growth.

- The judgment to distrust a number or a passing test before you build on it. You ask whether it is real, as a reflex.

- Clear communication with executives: you lead with the decision, keep your method in reserve, and hold up under pushback without either caving or digging in.

It Would Be Great If You Had

- Built specifically for AI agents as the consumer — MCP servers, agent harnesses, CLI tools, agent-readable docs, tool definitions, or evals for agent output.

- Experience with voice, audio, or real-time streaming systems.

- A track record of open-source work with real adoption.

- Time in a company with both a self-serve and an enterprise motion.

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager (Product-Led Growth)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity

We are hiring a Staff Product Manager focused on product-led growth. You will own the growth of the developer's journey from first touch to committed customer — as much of that funnel as the team's size calls for — and you will build the product that moves it. This is a founding-era team: the systems are young, the questions are not handed to you, and the person in this role defines what good looks like rather than executing someone else's definition. You report to the VP of Self-Serve and partner daily with engineering, design, developer relations, and the product analyst who owns the measurement behind your work.

What You’ll Do

- The growth of the PLG funnel — the metrics, the experiments that move them, and the product changes behind them. Your span may be one part of the funnel or the whole of it, and it can grow or narrow as the team does.

- The product across that experience — onboarding, the console, and the activation path a developer travels. You decide what ships and why; engineering builds it, and the developer-experience team owns the SDKs and docs you build on.

- The complete system your area runs on, stood up from scratch: the rhythms of business, data-driven optimization, and the experimentation platform. You build it yourself or in-house, or you research and deploy the best tools available.

- A weekly rhythm of shipping and measuring: a hypothesis, a change, an honest read of whether it worked, and the next bet. Not a roadmap of features shipped on faith.

- The cross-team work that falls between owners: with developer relations on acquisition and the shared developer platforms, with marketing on search and answer-engine presence, with sales and customer success on the handoff, and with the analyst on definitions and instrumentation.

You’ll Love This Role If You

- Get energized by being early — building the practice, not inheriting it.

- Have strong, evidence-backed opinions about product-led growth and are eager to be proven wrong by the data.

- Build things yourself. You prototype, you write the SQL to check a hunch, you stand up the landing page, you ship the fix. You do not wait for someone to build it for you.

- Reason at the altitude of a developer making an integration choice, increasingly with an AI agent in the loop.

- Are genuinely AI-native: you work with these tools all day, you know where they help and where they mislead, and you turn them on your own problems.

It’s Important to Us That You Have

- Product-led growth experience. This is mandatory. You have owned a PLG funnel metric — activation, conversion, retention, or acquisition — and moved it, in a product real users adopted without a salesperson.

- A track record as an all-around excellent PM: you set direction, you decide under uncertainty, you ship, and you can show the outcomes.

- The instinct and ability to build. You are technical enough to prototype, to reason about engineering tradeoffs, and to do your own analysis rather than wait on someone else's.

- Proven ability to stand up a complete system from scratch — the rhythms of business, the reporting and optimization, the experimentation platform — yourself or in-house, or by researching and deploying the right tools.

- Genuine AI fluency, judged by what you produce, not what you claim. You have built AI into your workflow past the first demo, you verify what it gives you, and you have a point of view on where it is still wrong.

- The judgment to distrust a number before you build on it. You ask whether a metric is real or an artifact of how it was measured, as a reflex.

- Clear communication with executives: you lead with the decision, hold your method in reserve, and hold up under pushback without either caving or digging in.

It Would Be Great If You Had

- Experience with a developer or API product, and fluency in how developers adopt SDKs and APIs.

- A view on how AI coding agents change discovery and integration, and what it means to have an agent as your user.

- A computer-science or engineering background, or a history of shipping your own side projects.

- Experience with the tools we use — Superset, Heap, GrowthBook, and the like.

- Time in a company that ran both a PLG and an enterprise motion, and understood how they feed each other.

jobs.title: Head of Editorial Content
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Role

Deepgram has deep technical expertise, unique customer insights, and a distinct point of view. Too much of that thinking never makes it into the world in a consistent, thoughtful way.

This role will work to uncover those ideas and turn them into a steady body of high-quality work that reinforces Deepgram’s narrative and gives people a reason to keep coming back to the company for insight.

Working closely with CEO, CMO, Head of Comms, and subject matter experts across the company, this person should build an editorial function that consistently turns Deepgram’s thinking into compelling stories, executive writing, customer stories, explainers, and recurring editorial series.

The goal is to help establish Deepgram as one of the defining voices in voice AI by publishing work that people actively seek out because it is genuinely insightful and worth their time.

What You’ll Do

  • Build editorial strategy and a content calendar that ladder up to Deepgram’s company narrative, key messages, and major moments.

  • Develop editorial themes around voice AI, enterprise AI, model development, customer impact, agents, and the future of human-AI interaction.

  • Mine stories across research, engineering, product, customers, GTM, and leadership; interview internal and external stakeholders to surface insights.

  • Write, edit, and produce core narrative materials, including executive posts, essays, customer stories, explainers, newsletters and launch support across formats and channels.

  • Create repeatable editorial franchises and formats that reinforce Deepgram’s narrative over time.

  • Make Deepgram’s technical, product, and customer stories more useful, more accessible, and more compelling.

  • Support major moments, including the fall event.

  • Partner with communications, product marketing, brand, design, video, and demand generation.

  • Build editorial processes that improve quality and consistency without making everything heavy.

What You’ll Bring

  • 8+ years in editorial, content, journalism, or a related field, with significant experience creating thoughtful content around complex technology.

  • A body of work that proves it: you can point to pieces that built a genuine point of view, not just filled a calendar.

  • Taste. You know what's actually interesting, what reads as credible, and how to make technical work feel relevant and compelling without flattening it into generic marketing.

  • Exceptional writing and editing range across formats—executive essays, customer stories, explainers, newsletters—with a high bar for clarity, substance, and craft.

  • Proven ability to produce high-quality work on a demanding schedule—you can sustain a newsroom-style cadence without letting quality slip, and you see consistency as a way to build authority rather than a reason to settle.

  • The instincts of a reporter: you can interview researchers, engineers, product people, and customers, get to the heart of complex material, and surface the insight worth publishing.

  • The ability to make technical depth accessible without losing substance, so the work stays useful to sophisticated readers while remaining readable for everyone else.

  • A track record of building repeatable editorial formats and franchises that hold quality and consistency over time, not one-off hits.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and a builder's mindset—you're energized by shaping an editorial function from the ground up, and can create lightweight processes that raise quality without making everything heavy.

  • A collaborative style, with experience partnering across communications, product marketing, brand, design, video, and demand gen, plus the relationship-building instinct to keep ideas surfacing from across the company.

  • Enough fluency in (or real curiosity about) technical subject matter to engage credibly with topics like model development, enterprise AI, and agents. You don't need to be an engineer, but curiosity here is non-negotiable.

Bonus points

  • A background in technology journalism or editorial—covering startups, AI, infrastructure, developer tools, or enterprise tech (think TechCrunch, VentureBeat, or a strong independent newsletter).

  • Time on an in-house editorial team at a company that treats content as a product (Stripe, Notion, GitHub, and the like).

  • Experience shaping a company's voice as a founder, executive, or ghostwriter in a technically complex environment.

  • Experience at an editorial agency or studio (Animalz or similar) working across complex technical clients, and ready to own a function in-house.

Why Deepgram

You will shape how the company at the center of the voice AI economy shows up in the world. The work you make will be seen by hundreds of thousands of developers and the enterprises building the future of voice. The system you build will outlast any single campaign. If you want your fingerprints on a brand as it steps into a new era, this is the role.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Model Evaluation & AI Systems
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity

Deepgram is looking for a Senior Software Engineer - Model Evaluation & AI Systems to join the team responsible for validating the quality of our speech, audio, and multilingual models before they reach customers.

This team owns the evaluation and quality assurance surfaces that ensure Deepgram's models — across speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and increasingly LLM- and multimodal-powered systems — meet their performance targets in both batch and streaming environments. We build the pipelines, harnesses, canaries, and test frameworks that catch regressions, hallucinations, and quality issues before they impact customers, and we partner closely with Research to turn model expectations into automated, reproducible, enforceable checks.

In this role, you'll define evaluation methodology and build the infrastructure that measures model quality at scale. You'll create evaluation pipelines, define pass/fail criteria grounded in Research benchmarks, and build the monitoring that keeps models honest in production. Your work provides the trusted signals that inform release and optimization decisions, and directly protects the customer experience.

We're looking for a strong engineer who is equally comfortable building test infrastructure and reasoning about model behavior. This role is aimed at senior engineers with broad instincts for quality, measurement, and automation; hands-on experience evaluating modern AI systems is a strong plus.

What You'll Do

  • Define and build evaluation methodologies for Deepgram's models, spanning speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and emerging LLM, RAG, agent, and multimodal systems.

  • Design, build, and maintain automated evaluation pipelines across batch and streaming (e.g. WER, runaway/hallucination detection, latency and time-to-first-byte), with a focus on correctness, reproducibility, and ease of adoption.

  • Build scalable, reproducible evaluation infrastructure — harnesses, orchestration, and result-aggregation pipelines — running against production models and, where needed, large GPU clusters.

  • Translate Research benchmarks and expected model metrics into automated, enforceable pass/fail gates.

  • Build and operate canaries and continuous-monitoring systems that detect quality regressions in production before they reach customers.

  • Partner with DevOps/Infra to stand up ephemeral test environments and results-aggregation infrastructure.

  • Work alongside Research, model training, inference, and product teams to provide trusted evaluation signals that inform release and optimization decisions.

  • Integrate evaluation and quality gates into CI/CD so quality is verified continuously, not manually.

  • Help raise the bar through code reviews, technical design discussions, and strong engineering and QA practices.

What We're Looking For

  • BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, AI, Applied Math, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • 5+ years of professional software or QA engineering experience, with a track record of shipping test infrastructure or evaluation systems (senior candidates with significantly deeper experience welcome).

  • Solid backend/scripting experience in a language such as Python, Rust, Go, or similar.

  • Experience designing and building automated test pipelines, evaluation frameworks, or data-processing systems.

  • Strong analytical skills and comfort reasoning about metrics, thresholds, and statistical variation in results — able to distinguish real regressions from noise.

  • Ability to take charge of ambiguous technical challenges and communicate effectively across research, engineering, and product teams.

Nice to Have / Ways to Stand Out

  • Hands-on experience evaluating modern AI systems such as LLMs, RAG pipelines, agents, or multimodal models, including model behavior analysis.

  • Experience with React Native or other cross-platform mobile frameworks for building tooling that's accessible beyond the desktop.

  • Experience building or improving evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, or ML infrastructure used by other teams or external users.

  • A strong appreciation for evaluation quality — correctness, reproducibility, and consistency across environments.

  • Experience with voice, audio, speech recognition, or real-time systems, and familiarity with metrics like WER, MOS, or latency/TTFB.

  • Prior involvement in open-source projects, through contributions, reviews, maintenance, or community engagement.

  • Experience acting as a technical bridge across teams or platforms (evaluation, training, inference, agent frameworks), combining architectural understanding with clear communication and influence.

  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, containerized/ephemeral environments, and monitoring tooling (e.g. Grafana, canaries, anomaly detection).

jobs.descriptionHtml:

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

About the Role

At Deepgram, data isn’t just fuel for our models, it’s a product in its own right. Our vertically integrated voice AI platform depends on strategically created, curated, and labeled audio: from original data collection and augmentation, to structured workflows and evaluation sets. These data pipelines support a range of cutting-edge technologies, including audio intelligence models, conversational voice agents, STT, and TTS.

We’re looking for a hands-on, systems-minded Program Manager to lead the design and execution of various voice data programs. This role is ideal for someone who thrives on building from scratch, someone who can take an abstract modeling goal or product need and turn it into a concrete data strategy and pipeline with tools, guidelines, and quality safeguards in place. This requires ownership to understand frontier research strategies, building custom style guides, prototyping new tools, and directly influencing how data shapes our products.

This is a role for builders, someone who can spot a gap, roll up their sleeves, and design the solution. You’ll be at the center of Deepgram’s model development cycle, working across Research, Engineering, and Product, and you’ll be elbow-deep in both the day-to-day execution and the systems thinking required to scale it.

This role reports to the VP of Data Operations.

What You’ll Own:

  • Design, launch, and own end-to-end data workflows: from raw audio ingestion to production-ready datasets

  • Build and evolve labeling specs, style guides, and instructional documentation for global annotation teams

  • Identify opportunities for better tooling, automation, and workflow optimization, and lead their implementation

  • Translate product goals and model requirements into data creation strategies, deciding what to build, how to build it, and why it matters for product impact

  • Own the full lifecycle for your domains — customer expectations, data acquisition, preparation, scaling, provenance, and evaluation — and be accountable for the model outcome, not just the data hand-off.

  • Prototype and deploy data tools and infrastructure

  • Collaborate with Research and Engineering to align data collection with model training architecture and downstream product impact

  • Track advancements in speech AI research and evolving market use cases to inform labeling approaches and data design priorities

  • Partner with QA and Evaluation leads to deliver high-quality, human-in-the-loop datasets and benchmarks

  • Manage and mentor data vendors, freelancers, and potentially internal ICs as the team grows

  • Track throughput, data quality, and vendor performance

  • Drive continuous improvement in speed, cost-efficiency, and quality across all data operations

  • Curate and refine datasets to align with specific product goals, linguistic coverage, or research hypotheses

What We're Looking For

  • Experience owning data, ML, or operations programs end-to-end in program/project or product management.

  • Fluency working directly with technical teams; you can hold a conversation about data quality, evaluation, and model impact.

  • Systems thinking, understanding how decisions propagate across a system, reason up from fundamentals instead of defaulting to convention, and design solutions that hold up as things scale.

  • A track record of prioritization under constraint — deciding what to fund, what to cut, and how to sequence it.

  • Strong operating instincts: you scope, sequence, assign, and ship, and nothing stalls because someone didn't know the next step.

  • Demonstrated ability to design and build scalable processes, not just manage existing ones

It would be great if you also had:

  • Direct exposure to speech/audio, ASR, or TTS data, and the specific nuances of multilingual, code-switched, low-resource, or domain-specific data.

  • Experience with active-learning or data-selection approaches

  • Startup or high-ambiguity experience

You’ll Love This Role If You

  • Believe that data is a product, not just a resource, and you want to help define what great voice data looks like

  • Enjoy turning experimental ideas into robust, repeatable systems that can scale to production

  • Thrive in ambiguity and take initiative without waiting for perfect specs, preferring action over perfection and iteration over indecision

More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.




COMPANY OPERATING RHYTHM

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.




ABOUT THE ROLE

At Deepgram, data isn’t just fuel for our models, it’s a product in its own right. Our vertically integrated voice AI platform depends on strategically created, curated, and labeled audio: from original data collection and augmentation, to structured workflows and evaluation sets. These data pipelines support a range of cutting-edge technologies, including audio intelligence models, conversational voice agents, STT, and TTS.

We’re looking for a hands-on, systems-minded Program Manager to lead the design and execution of various voice data programs. This role is ideal for someone who thrives on building from scratch, someone who can take an abstract modeling goal or product need and turn it into a concrete data strategy and pipeline with tools, guidelines, and quality safeguards in place. This requires ownership to understand frontier research strategies, building custom style guides, prototyping new tools, and directly influencing how data shapes our products.

This is a role for builders, someone who can spot a gap, roll up their sleeves, and design the solution. You’ll be at the center of Deepgram’s model development cycle, working across Research, Engineering, and Product, and you’ll be elbow-deep in both the day-to-day execution and the systems thinking required to scale it.

This role reports to the VP of Data Operations.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN:

 - Design, launch, and own end-to-end data workflows: from raw audio ingestion to production-ready datasets

 - Build and evolve labeling specs, style guides, and instructional documentation for global annotation teams

 - Identify opportunities for better tooling, automation, and workflow optimization, and lead their implementation

 - Translate product goals and model requirements into data creation strategies, deciding what to build, how to build it, and why it matters for product impact

 - Own the full lifecycle for your domains — customer expectations, data acquisition, preparation, scaling, provenance, and evaluation — and be accountable for the model outcome, not just the data hand-off.

 - Prototype and deploy data tools and infrastructure

 - Collaborate with Research and Engineering to align data collection with model training architecture and downstream product impact

 - Track advancements in speech AI research and evolving market use cases to inform labeling approaches and data design priorities

 - Partner with QA and Evaluation leads to deliver high-quality, human-in-the-loop datasets and benchmarks

 - Manage and mentor data vendors, freelancers, and potentially internal ICs as the team grows

 - Track throughput, data quality, and vendor performance

 - Drive continuous improvement in speed, cost-efficiency, and quality across all data operations

 - Curate and refine datasets to align with specific product goals, linguistic coverage, or research hypotheses




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience owning data, ML, or operations programs end-to-end in program/project or product management.

 - Fluency working directly with technical teams; you can hold a conversation about data quality, evaluation, and model impact.

 - Systems thinking, understanding how decisions propagate across a system, reason up from fundamentals instead of defaulting to convention, and design solutions that hold up as things scale.

 - A track record of prioritization under constraint — deciding what to fund, what to cut, and how to sequence it.

 - Strong operating instincts: you scope, sequence, assign, and ship, and nothing stalls because someone didn't know the next step.

 - Demonstrated ability to design and build scalable processes, not just manage existing ones




IT WOULD BE GREAT IF YOU ALSO HAD:

 - Direct exposure to speech/audio, ASR, or TTS data, and the specific nuances of multilingual, code-switched, low-resource, or domain-specific data.

 - Experience with active-learning or data-selection approaches

 - Startup or high-ambiguity experience




YOU’LL LOVE THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Believe that data is a product, not just a resource, and you want to help define what great voice data looks like

 - Enjoy turning experimental ideas into robust, repeatable systems that can scale to production

 - Thrive in ambiguity and take initiative without waiting for perfect specs, preferring action over perfection and iteration over indecision

There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

Our Customer Success team — The Heartbeat of Deepgram — sits at the intersection of customers, product, and growth. We don't just "manage accounts." We make Deepgram succeed inside our customers' environments by combining deep technical expertise, commercial instinct, and an AI-native way of working — and by building the systems that make the whole team's work compound over time.

 

A Customer Success Engineer is a hands-on partner who drives adoption, solves hard technical problems, uncovers expansion, and owns a portfolio of strategic enterprise accounts end to end.

Who You Are

You're not a traditional CSM or Technical Account Manager. You operate at the intersection of three competencies, and you're genuinely strong across all three:

 

  1. Expert technical consulting — you run demos, guide architecture discussions, troubleshoot integrations, and help customers deploy AI-driven solutions. No coding required, but you're fluent in APIs, developer workflows, and real technical conversations.

  2. Strategic account management — you build trust from individual developers up to CTOs, own the full customer lifecycle, and turn technical adoption into commercial growth.

  3. AI-native operating model — AI is how you work, not a tool you occasionally reach for. When you hit recurring work, your instinct is to build the system that removes it.

 

You may have been a Technical Account Manager, Solutions or Sales Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Implementation Engineer, strategic CSM, or Product Manager. Whatever your path, you're probably strongest in one or two of these competencies — but you can demonstrate all three, and you're eager for a role where you deploy them concurrently.

 

You thrive on bringing definition to ambiguity. You form a point of view and bring a recommendation rather than staying in open-ended discovery mode. You're comfortable operating outside your comfort zone, you question the status quo, and you learn fast.

What You'll Do

  • Serve as the technical advisor and strategic owner for a portfolio of enterprise accounts, partnering with everyone from developers to CIOs and CTOs.

  • Own the full customer lifecycle: onboarding, adoption, technical enablement, expansion, and advocacy.

  • Drive adoption through live demos, workshops, architecture guidance, troubleshooting, and best-practice recommendations — making Deepgram successful inside the customer's environment.

  • Run discovery continuously: surface customer problems, understand their business impact, and translate them into actionable requirements for product and engineering.

  • Identify and scope expansion (cross-sell, upsell, multi-product) in partnership with Sales, and lead executive business reviews and joint planning sessions.

  • Act as the voice of the customer internally — influencing roadmap, GTM strategy, and the tools we build to support customers.

  • Track adoption, usage, health, and expansion to drive outcomes; travel to customer sites as needed.

  • Operate AI-first by default, and build tools, agents, and workflows that eliminate recurring work for you and the broader CS team. Your impact is measured by the leverage you create, not just the accounts you serve.

What We're Looking For

  • Significant experience in technical, customer-facing roles — TAM, sales/solutions engineering, enterprise CS with a strong technical focus, implementation, or forward-deployed work — at API-driven, developer-first, or AI companies. For most people that's roughly 7+ years, but we care more about the shape of your experience than the exact number.

  • A track record that blends customer ownership with technical depth: solution design, hands-on troubleshooting, and commercial growth.

  • Hands-on experience running demos, POCs, or technical workshops with enterprise customers — leading them, not just attending.

  • Demonstrated success identifying and landing expansion in complex enterprise accounts.

  • Fluency discussing APIs, integrations, and developer workflows, and troubleshooting L1-style issues (no coding required, but genuinely conversant — not hand-waving).

  • Experience engaging both technical stakeholders (developers, architects) and executive buyers (CIO, CTO, VP Engineering).

  • Exceptional communication, influence, and relationship-building — concise and structured, across technical and business audiences.

  • Something you've built — a tool, agent, script, or workflow — that permanently eliminated recurring work. In your application, tell us what it was, what it replaced, and what it's still doing today.

  • An AI-native operating model: specific workflows that structurally depend on AI, and a clear account of how you'd rebuild them if those tools disappeared tomorrow.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in machine learning, voice AI, cloud infrastructure, or developer-first technologies.

  • A background spanning solutions engineering, TAM, or L1 support alongside CS responsibilities.

  • Working fluency with automation, scripting, or agent-building (Python, TypeScript, workflow tools, agent frameworks, or equivalent). You don't need to be a software engineer — just dangerous enough to ship working systems.

Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

Deepgram is the Voice AI platform powering the next generation of mission-critical government systems, including contact center modernization, benefits and case processing, and real-time speech applications across Defense, Federal Civilian, Intelligence Community, and State, Local, and Education (SLED) agencies. As we scale our federal footprint, Systems Integrators and Primes, cloud hyperscalers, and channel partners are our highest-leverage route to market. Our partners sit at the center of the AI modernization programs happening inside every federal agency. We are hiring a Federal Partner Manager to build, grow, and scale Deepgram's federal partner network from the ground up.

This is a builder role. You will own the strategy and execution for our named Systems Integrator and Prime practices alongside strategic hyperscaler alliances and channel partners, and you will define what a world-class AI-native federal partner motion looks like at Deepgram. You will design and drive sell-to, sell-through, and sell-with motions, land joint solutions inside each partner's delivery and capture organization, and deliver measurable partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue. You will not run a traditional partner program. You will run an AI-first approach: leveraging agents, automation, and data to operate at 10x the scale of a conventional federal alliances team.

If you are a partner leader who thrives on whitespace, has a proven record scaling federal SI/prime and hyperscaler relationships from zero, and genuinely wants to use AI to reinvent how federal partner GTM is done, this role is for you.

What you'll do

  • Work closely with the VP of Federal and own the federal partner strategy end-to-end. Build and execute the named-account strategy for federal and strategic hyperscaler partners; including joint value propositions, partner account plans, solution plays, and governance cadences with each partner's alliances and delivery leadership.

  • Drive sell-to, sell-through, and sell-with motions:

  • Sell-to: Land Deepgram as the embedded speech/voice AI layer inside each SI/prime's own AI platforms, mission software factories, and delivery accelerators.

  • Sell-through: Stand up repeatable SI/prime-led offerings (agency contact center transformation, DoD voice-enabled C2/ISR analytics, benefits-processing voice AI) that the partner takes to its agency customers under its own contract vehicle.

  • Sell-with: Co-sell into named federal accounts with SI and hyperscaler account teams, owning joint pipeline, forecast, and deal execution alongside Deepgram's Federal Account Executives.

  • Build a measurable partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline. Set quarterly and annual targets with each partner, instrument the pipeline end-to-end, and own the number.

  • Work alongside the partner team to build the federal partner enablement and credential/certification program. Align Deepgram's Applied Engineering/FDE playbook with SI and hyperscaler delivery teams.

  • Create the joint solutions. Work with product, engineering, solutions architects, and each partner's industry/mission practices to package reference architectures, delivery playbooks, and offerings specific to Defense/DoW, Federal Civilian, IC, and SLED.

  • Enable at scale. Design and launch partner enablement — technical certifications, sales plays, GovCloud demo environments, and solution-led training — plus contract-vehicle placement (GSA MAS, NASA SEWP, CIO-SP3, GWACs); so hundreds of partner sellers and practitioners can position, demo, and deliver Deepgram.

  • Be AI-native in how you work. This is a defining part of the role. You will build and deploy AI systems — agents, automations, data pipelines — to do the job of a conventional 5–10 person federal alliances team. Examples:

  • Agents that monitor SI/prime alliance news, contract awards, GSA Schedule updates, and account movements, and auto-draft briefs.

  • Automated partner-sourced pipeline hygiene, account mapping, and co-sell attribution using Deepgram's CRM, Slack, and partner portals.

  • AI-generated partner-specific collateral, solution briefs, and enablement content tuned to each partner's agency vertical.

  • Data pipelines that join Deepgram's CRM with partner account maps and public procurement signals (SAM.gov, USASpending) to surface the next-best co-sell opportunity every week.

  • Represent Deepgram externally. Be the senior face of Deepgram in alliance QBRs, joint executive briefings, federal AI summits (AFCEA, ACT-IAC, GITEC), and industry events. Carry a consistent point of view on where federal voice AI is going and where Deepgram fits in the SI/prime agenda.

  • Partner cross-functionally inside Deepgram. Work closely with Federal Account Executives (Defense, Federal Civilian, IC, SLED), Applied Engineering, Capture/Proposal, Government Affairs, and Legal to remove friction and accelerate partner-driven revenue.

  • Report on what matters. Own the federal partner dashboard: partner-sourced pipeline, partner-influenced pipeline, joint wins, certified resources, joint solutions launched, and partner NPS; with crisp, honest narratives each month and quarter.

What you bring

  • Must be a U.S. citizen.

  • 7+ years in partner management, alliances, business development, or federal enterprise sales — with at least 3–5 years directly owning SI/prime or hyperscaler federal relationships.

  • Demonstrated track record of building sell-to, sell-through, and sell-with motions with named federal partners and delivering measurable partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue.

  • Experience scaling a federal partnership from early-stage or zero — not inheriting a mature program.

  • Strong command of how federal SIs/primes actually operate: capture teams, delivery centers, COEs, contract vehicles, teaming agreements, and how deals get sourced and staffed inside them.

  • Fluency with the federal AI landscape — LLMs, agentic AI, mission software factories, FedRAMP/DoD Impact Level authorization pathways, and hyperscaler federal co-sell motions.

  • Hands-on AI-native operator. You personally use AI tools every day — not as a talking point. You have built automations, agents, or data workflows that replaced meaningful human effort, and you can show us.

  • Excellent executive presence — comfortable opening and advancing conversations with partner SVPs, federal practice leads, and Deepgram's own executive team.

  • Analytical rigor. You instrument what you own, tell the truth with data, and translate numbers into decisions.

  • Self-directed, high-ownership, and comfortable operating in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

It would be great if you also had

  • An active security clearance is a bonus, not a requirement.

  • Existing strong relationships inside at least two of SI or Prime partner organizations.

  • Direct experience launching a joint federal offering or solution that produced repeatable agency engagements.

  • Background in speech, voice AI, CCaaS, or adjacent domains (AWS Connect GovCloud, Genesys Government, NICE, ServiceNow Federal).

  • Experience building internal AI tooling — agents, RAG systems, CRM automations — for a revenue team.

Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.

 - 7+ years in partner management, alliances, business development, or federal enterprise sales — with at least 3–5 years directly owning SI/prime or hyperscaler federal relationships.

 - Experience scaling a federal partnership from early-stage or zero — not inheriting a mature program.

 - Strong command of how federal SIs/primes actually operate: capture teams, delivery centers, COEs, contract vehicles, teaming agreements, and how deals get sourced and staffed inside them.

 - Fluency with the federal AI landscape — LLMs, agentic AI, mission software factories, FedRAMP/DoD Impact Level authorization pathways, and hyperscaler federal co-sell motions.

 - Self-directed, high-ownership, and comfortable operating in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

 - An active security clearance is a bonus, not a requirement.

 - Existing strong relationships inside at least two of SI or Prime partner organizations.

 - Direct experience launching a joint federal offering or solution that produced repeatable agency engagements.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

Deepgram is the Voice AI platform powering the next generation of government contact centers, benefits and case processing, and real-time speech applications. Federal Civilian agencies — VA, HHS, DHS, SSA, USDA, Treasury, DOJ, GSA, CBP, USCIS, FEMA, TSA, IRS, CMS, and FDA — represent for Deepgram what enterprise Global 2000 accounts represent commercially: the core buying constituency for mission-critical voice AI. We are hiring a Strategic Account Executive, Federal Civilian Agencies to build, grow, and scale Deepgram's civilian agency book of business from the ground up.

This is a builder role, directly reporting to the VP of Federal. You will own the strategy and execution for named civilian agency accounts, and you will define what a world-class AI-native federal seller looks like at Deepgram. You will design and drive direct, partner-assisted, and channel-enabled motions, land Deepgram inside real mission programs, and deliver measurable pipeline and closed revenue. You will not run a traditional territory. You will run an AI-first approach: leveraging agents, automation, and data to operate like a seller with a research and BD team behind you.

If you are a seller who thrives on whitespace, has a proven record building federal civilian relationships from zero, and genuinely wants to use AI to reinvent how federal selling is done, this role is for you.

What you'll do

  • Own the Federal Civilian go-to-market strategy. Build and execute a named-account strategy for target agencies; including agency mission mapping, account plans, and stakeholder engagement across program, technical, and contracting stakeholders.

  • Drive direct, partner-assisted, and channel-enabled motions:

  • Direct: Prospect, qualify, and close opportunities directly with agency program offices and mission owners.

  • Partner-assisted: Co-sell with Deepgram's Federal Partnerships team and named SIs/primes already embedded in an agency's delivery contract.

  • Channel-enabled: Route and manage deals through GSA Schedule resellers to meet agency purchasing requirements.

  • Build a measurable, quota-carrying pipeline. Meet quarterly and annual targets, instrument the pipeline end-to-end in CRM, and own the number.

  • Navigate government contracting mechanics — RFIs, RFPs, sole-source/J&A justifications, GSA Schedule ordering — as a normal part of the sales motion, not an afterthought.

  • Build the win strategy for each opportunity. Work with Sales and Applied Engineering to develop compliant, compelling responses to competitive and sole-source opportunities.

  • Be AI-native in how you work. This is a defining part of the role. Examples:

  • Agents that monitor agency budget, RFP, and award signals (SAM.gov, USASpending, agency IT modernization roadmaps) and auto-draft account briefs.

  • Automated pipeline hygiene and next-best-action recommendations tied to CRM.

  • AI-generated, agency-specific outreach and proposal content.

  • Data pipelines that join CRM with public procurement data to surface the next opportunity before an RFP drops.

  • Represent Deepgram externally at civilian-agency industry days, conferences (ACT-IAC, AFCEA, GITEC), and customer events. Carry a consistent point of view on where federal voice AI adoption is heading.

  • Partner cross-functionally inside Deepgram. Work closely with Federal Partnerships, Applied Engineering and Legal to remove friction and accelerate civilian-agency revenue.

  • Report on what matters. Own your pipeline dashboard: sourced pipeline, partner-influenced pipeline, closed/won revenue, and forecast accuracy; with crisp, honest narratives each month and quarter.

What you bring

  • Must be a U.S. citizen.

  • 5+ years of full-cycle sales experience, with at least 3 years directly selling to Federal Civilian agencies (enterprise SaaS/technology sales strongly preferred).

  • Demonstrated track record of meeting or exceeding quota in complex, multi-stakeholder federal sales cycles.

  • Experience building a federal territory or book of business from early-stage or zero — not inheriting a mature book.

  • Strong command of how civilian agencies buy: program offices, contracting officers, GSA Schedule ordering, BPAs/IDIQs, and how deals actually get funded and staffed.

  • Fluency with the broader federal AI/modernization landscape; EO 14058 customer experience mandates FedRAMP, agentic AI, and CCaaS/contact-center ecosystems.

  • Hands-on AI-native operator. You use AI tools daily, have built automations or workflows that replaced meaningful manual effort, and can show us.

  • Excellent executive presence and comfortable engaging senior government stakeholders and Deepgram's own leadership.

  • Analytical rigor. You instrument your pipeline, tell the truth with data, and translate numbers into decisions.

  • Self-directed, high-ownership, and comfortable operating in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

It would be great if you also had

  • An active security clearance is a bonus, not a requirement — helpful for select civilian agency components with sensitive programs, though the large majority of Federal Civilian work does not require one.

  • Existing relationships with stakeholders inside at least two target civilian agencies, and/or the reseller ecosystem.

  • Direct experience closing a novel or first-of-kind deal at a civilian agency.

  • Background selling speech/voice AI, contact-center, or developer-first API products.

  • Familiarity with sales methodologies such as Shipley or Solution Selling in government contexts.

  • Experience building internal AI tooling for a sales or revenue workflow.

jobs.title: Senior Pre-Sales Solutions Engineer (Australia)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

Note: this role is based out of Australia and will service the APAC region.

 

Opportunity

Deepgram is expanding across APAC and operating a follow-the-sun model. We are hiring a Pre-Sales Solutions Engineer in Australia to win complex technical evaluations, design clear solution paths, and drive repeatable adoption for strategic accounts. Our strategic Account Executives do not hand off their customers after the first sale, so you will partner long term across discovery, POC, production launch, and expansion. You will focus on pre-sales, and you will often step into post-sales style work when the stakes are high and continuity matters.

 

About Applied Engineering at Deepgram

Applied Engineering blends what many companies split into Solutions Engineering, Architecture, Consulting, and Senior Technical Support. We are builders and communicators who bridge sales and engineering. We help customers move from problem to production with speed, clarity, and measurable outcomes.

 

What You Will Do

  • Lead technical discovery for strategic opportunities. Map business goals to measurable technical success criteria and an evaluation plan.

  • Design, scope, and execute POCs that prove value. Define datasets, metrics, and timelines that land a clear technical win.

  • Build lightweight prototypes, sample integrations, and demos using Deepgram SDKs and APIs.

  • Advise on architecture for accuracy, latency, scalability, and cost. Cover cloud, self-hosted, hybrid, and data residency needs.

  • Run security and compliance threads common in APAC. Prepare crisp responses for Singapore PDPA, Japan APPI, Korea PIPA, Australia’s Privacy Act, and India’s DPDP Act.

  • Triage and debug issues during evaluations. Collaborate with Product, Engineering, and Support to unblock customers quickly.

  • Create reusable assets that scale. Turn repeated requests into working samples, reference architectures, runbooks, and field guides.

  • Partner with Solutions Architects and Support for seamless continuity after initial wins. Stay involved through expansion phases when needed.

  • Enable the field. Collaborate with AEs, CSMs, and partners on positioning, demos, and technical validation for priority use cases.

 

Regional Expectations

  • Based in Australia with strong overlap to customer business hours across East Asia, Southeast Asia, and ANZ.

  • Excellent written and spoken English. Additional Asian languages are a strong plus.

  • Familiarity with procurement, InfoSec, and data privacy expectations across APAC.

  • Ability to travel within the region for key customer milestones. Estimated travel 10 to 20 percent.

 

Your First 90 Days

Ramp approach for this role Ramping mirrors the Solutions Architect plan, with explicit ticket work and earlier support for strategic Account Executives. In the first weeks you will pick up low-risk customer tickets to learn our systems and support flow, then progress to pre-sales escalations tied to active evaluations.

First 30 days

  • Ramp on Deepgram’s product surface area, platform APIs, SDKs, evaluation methodology, and security review materials.

  • Shadow strategic discovery and POC calls across APAC time zones.

  • Triage and resolve low-risk tickets with a Solutions Architect or Support partner. Focus on reproductions, log and trace collection, SDK setup issues, and clear notes and handoffs.

  • Publish one internal field guide that clarifies a common APAC pre-sales topic (for example data residency, telephony capture, or evaluation metrics).

By day 60

  • Own two evaluations end to end with defined success criteria and timelines.

  • Serve as the named technical partner for one or two strategic AEs. Run weekly technical deal reviews and prepare objection-handling packs.

  • Take point on higher-signal tickets related to your evaluations, coordinating fast fixes with Product, Engineering, and Support.

  • Deliver one live demo that becomes a reusable asset for the region. Pair with a Solutions Architect on a production launch to learn handoffs and escalation paths.

By day 90

  • Act as the primary pre-sales technical owner for several opportunities and expansions within strategic accounts.

  • Close at least one complex technical win with a measurable impact on revenue.

  • Lead one customer architecture workshop that documents a reference plan for production rollout or expansion.

  • Convert repeated ticket patterns into a runbook, sample, or accelerator and present a short readout on the impact.

 

You Will Thrive Here If You

  • Enjoy the mix of customer conversations and hands-on building.

  • Can move from whiteboard to working code and back without losing the thread.

  • Communicate clearly with executives and deeply with engineers.

  • Value speed with rigor and crisp documentation.

  • Like winning together across regions and functions.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 5 or more years in Solutions Engineering or a similar customer-facing technical role focused on pre-sales.

  • Professional software engineering experience in at least one language such as JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, or Rust. You can build POCs and tools that real users run.

  • Hands-on experience with modern cloud platforms. Comfortable with Docker, Kubernetes, networking fundamentals, and secure API design.

  • Proven track record leading POCs for enterprise customers and earning the technical win.

  • Clear written and verbal communication across both technical and executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with speech recognition, TTS, voice quality analysis, or AI agents that orchestrate LLMs.

  • Familiarity with telephony and real-time media concepts such as SIP, WebRTC, streaming, and WebSocket integrations.

  • Experience with self-hosted and hybrid deployments, including Helm-based installs and production observability.

  • Strong understanding of authentication, authorization, and data residency topics that appear in APAC enterprise reviews.

  • Fluency in an additional Asian language such as Japanese, Korean, Mandarin, or Hindi.

 

How We Work

  • Remote across APAC with periodic regional meetups.

  • Close partnership with AEs, SAs, Product, and Engineering to support continuous coverage across APAC, EMEA, and the Americas.

  • Shared playbooks, defined escalation paths, and measurable SLAs.

 

Interview Process

  • Recruiter screen focused on experience, motivations, and logistics.

  • Hiring manager conversation focused on technical depth and customer impact.

  • Practical assessment that mirrors real work. Expect discovery, solution design, and a short hands-on exercise.

  • Panel interviews with cross-functional partners.

  • Live demo and architecture walkthrough of a past technical win. Show your approach to success criteria, trade offs, and outcomes.

If this sounds like you, we would love to meet you!

Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.
