There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

As a Senior Product Marketing Manager, Solutions Marketing at Deepgram, you will be our first dedicated solutions marketer. Enterprises don't buy speech models, they buy outcomes: patient intake that never misses a medication name, drive-thrus that get the order right, federal deployments that run air-gapped. You'll translate our platform into the solution narratives, first-call decks, and proof that make those outcomes obvious to buyers, and you'll build the systems that produce them repeatably, not one asset at a time.

This role sits within Product Marketing, reports to the Senior Manager of Partner, Customer, and Solutions Marketing, and works most closely with marketing and sales. You'll also partner with Applied Engineering and DevRel on demos, Demand Gen on vertical campaigns, and Partner and Customer Marketing on proof and distribution.

What You'll Do

  • Own the solutions bill of materials end-to-end: for each priority use case and vertical, build and maintain the narrative, first-call deck, solution brief, hero demo script, battlecard, proof points, and web copy, refreshed quarterly. If sellers are not using it, it does not count.

  • Build use-case-first messaging with vertical multipliers: anchor on what buyers deploy (voice agents for support, clinical documentation, ordering, intake) and layer verticals on top (healthcare and pharma, federal and public sector, financial services, CX and restaurants)

  • Lead the solutions layer of every major launch: own the "what this unlocks for your industry" story, including named accuracy metrics that set the category's measuring stick

  • Be the voice of the market: mine sales calls, win-loss, and usage patterns for messaging evidence; sit in prospect calls; turn deployments into segment proof points with Customer Marketing

  • Feed demand gen and the field: hand campaign-ready narratives and landing-page messaging to Demand Gen, package enablement with GTM Enablement, and route solutions content through co-marketing with Partner Marketing.

  • Own competitive positioning by segment against AI-native voice platforms, hyperscaler models, and legacy vendors

  • Build the solutions content engine as a repeatable AI-powered system (intake, production, distribution, measurement) and publish the reusable pieces so PMM peers self-serve from what you build

You'll Love This Role If You

  • Have built solutions, portfolio, or vertical marketing programs before and can show us the work: solution briefs you wrote, first-call decks sellers ran with, plays that moved pipeline

  • Think of solutions marketing as a revenue function, measured in pipeline, win rates, and deal velocity

  • Go deep on technical products: you'll run our APIs, build simple demos from our docs, and hold your own with Product and Engineering

  • Work AI-first by default: you prototype with AI before you brief, and you build workflows instead of repeating tasks

  • Can write for a CTO and a CX ops leader in the same week without either noticing a template

  • Are excited about voice AI and want to define how a category gets bought

It's Important To Us That You Have

  • 5–7 years of solutions, product, or portfolio marketing experience in B2B SaaS, with at least one technical or API-first product; this is a senior role

  • A portfolio of solutions marketing work to present during the interview: solution briefs, first-call decks, battlecards, sales plays. We will ask to see it.

  • Proven use of AI to accelerate workflows, content creation, and program scale; daily AI use is the baseline, building reusable systems with AI is the bar

  • A track record of translating a multi-product portfolio into segment narratives with measurable pipeline or win-rate impact

  • Hands-on enablement experience: content sellers actually used, with the feedback loops to prove it

  • Demand gen partnership fluency: you understand pipeline mechanics and have handed campaign-ready messaging to a demand gen team

  • Excellent writing that survives contact with technical reviewers and enterprise buyers alike

It Would Be Great If You Had

  • Experience in voice AI, conversational AI, CCaaS, or speech technology

  • Background marketing into a regulated vertical (healthcare, federal, financial services)

  • Analyst relations exposure or benchmark/named-metric storytelling experience

  • Public speaking or webinar presenter experience

  • Track record in high-growth startups where you built the function's systems from scratch

We're an AI-native team. We expect AI to be woven into how you work, not something you reach for occasionally.

This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

Staff Web Engineer Marketing

About the role

Deepgram builds foundational voice AI and deepgram.com is where the world meets it. The site is our digital front door, showcasing our products, brand moments, and pricing information, and it drives the company's self-serve revenue.

We're hiring a Staff Web Engineer to own the site's code for the long haul. Deepgram.com is entering its next chapter. We are fully refreshing the experience top to bottom. You'll be the person who knows the site inside out. You'll own the repo, the architecture, the Sanity environments, and the QA bar — and act as the code-review gate for day-to-day page and content work. The team is small but scaling. You will be working on the Web team reporting into the Senior Web Manager and closely collaborating with product, marketing, sales, and external development partners.

Most critically, as an AI company, you must be AI-native. Agents and AI tooling are your go-to in how you choose to build, review, and QA. We are aiming to build a machine-first, voice-first site experience. It’s an exciting time to join the web team.

What you'll do

  • Own the deepgram.com codebase end to end — the Next.js application (front and back end), the GitHub repo, branching and CI/CD, and code review

  • Optimize and maintain Sanity CMS architecture — schemas, the reusable module library, the staging and production environments and publishing workflow

  • Run the global design system, component library, Vercel platform and spearhead AI integrations. Experienced with global CSS systems.

  • Build and run the site's QA program — starting with a well-structured and scalable staging environment that keeps a marketing site launch-ready at all times

  • Lead internationalization and localization efforts — language-locale URL and routing architecture, hreflang, and the path from i18n plumbing to localized (l10n) content

  • Assist in technical SEO — site architecture, redirects, Core Web Vitals — with on-page SEO executed by content partners inside your review gate

  • Ensure LLM discoverability (AEO) — the site's structured data, metadata, and content architecture must serve answer engines as well as people

  • Technical infrastructure for experimentation — develop the mechanisms to support the site's experimentation program

  • Marketing Ops partnership — implementation of forms, gated content, and attribution instrumentation (GTM, GA4, HubSpot)

  • Cybersecurity posture — maintain security and run routine safety audits across dependencies and scripts

  • High-velocity shipping — ship complex site improvements and launch campaign pages in a product-driven atmosphere

  • AI-native workflow — use agents in your daily build process and create tooling for safe marketing publishing

We are looking for candidates with:

  • Marketing web development background — ownership of marketing sites, not just product surfaces

  • Enterprise repository ownership: branching strategy, CI/CD, and a strong code-review culture

  • Headless CMS architecture — Next.js with Sanity strongly preferred

  • Modern React ecosystem for the web

  • Vercel as a production platform

  • AI-native development — ability to demonstrate concrete use of AI agents and tooling in your workflow

  • High level of ownership & accountability — a hand raiser who’s ready to join an ambitious team and company

  • Technical leadership — directing or reviewing the work of agency developers

Our ideal candidates also have:

  • Prior experience with internationalization (i18n/l10n): URL architecture, locale routing, and multi-region infrastructure

  • Familiarity with A/B testing on production marketing sites

  • Interest in voice AI and the future of voice-interactive web experiences

Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.

jobs.title: Global Head of Real Estate and Workplace
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

About the Role

We are growing our geographic footprint and opening multiple workspaces and event spaces across the U.S. and internationally. Most of these locations serve a dual purpose. They are working spaces for Deepgram employees and public event venues that host meetups, hackathons, and customer and developer gatherings. Designing and operating space that does both well is a key aspect of this role.

Right now, real estate decisions, office openings, construction projects, and facilities operations are spread across many people. We need one responsible and experienced owner who knows how to do this all end to end. Someone who can read a lease, walk a construction site, manage a vendor, and think clearly about how a space shapes culture, brand, and community.

As Global Head of Real Estate and Workplace, you will take full ownership of Deepgram's physical spaces from site selection through to operational, welcoming offices. You will find potential real estate, negotiate and manage leases, run buildout projects, stand up facilities operations, and build the repeatable playbook we use to open and run every Deepgram location. Then you will hire and lead a small team to run it with you.

This is a player-coach role. You will be in the work, not above it, and you will build the function as you go.

What You'll Own

Requirements Scoping & Internal Stakeholder Management

  • Converting the CEO and executive team’s vision into a documented program for each site

  • Gathering requirements across Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Developer Relations, People, IT, Security, and Finance to determine how each space will be used and what it needs to solve for

  • Reconciling competing requests into a single prioritized brief, secure executive approval, and own that brief as the source of truth for architects, general contractors, and all subsequent change decisions

Capacity & Space Planning

  • Occupancy forecasting and space programming against the company headcount plan, in partnership with Finance and People

  • Recommendations on the size, timing, and location of new and expanded space, grounded in utilization data rather than anecdote

  • The tradeoff at each site between event capacity, collaboration space, and focus work, documented and revisited as headcount changes

Real Estate & Leasing

  • Site selection, tours, and location recommendations as we evaluate new and expanded spaces

  • Lease negotiation and renewals, partnering with Finance and Legal on LOIs, term sheets, insurance needs, and commercial terms, including tenant improvement allowances, free rent, escalations, letters of credit and security deposits, restoration and holdover obligations, assignment and sublease rights, and expansion and termination flexibility

  • Analysis of lease versus license, coworking, and short-term venue alternatives in markets where a long-term commitment is not yet warranted

  • International site selection and leasing, including engagement of local counsel and brokers, country-specific code and accessibility standards, and coordination with Finance, People, and Legal on the entity, tax, and employment implications of each location

  • Partnership with Accounting on lease classification and ASC 842 treatment, and delivery of the underlying data Finance needs for budgeting, forecasting, and audit

  • Landlord and broker relationships, and ownership of all real estate documentation and key dates

Construction & Buildout

  • End-to-end project management of office buildouts, from design intent through permitting, construction, and move-in

  • Coordination of architects, general contractors, designers, and trades — holding scope, budget, and timeline

  • Design and delivery of assembly and event space, including occupancy classification and egress, load-in and rigging, AV and streaming infrastructure, acoustics, power and network capacity for large gatherings, and commercial or catered food service

  • Permitting, code, accessibility, and safety compliance across every project

Facilities & Workplace Operations

  • Day-to-day operations across all offices: supplies, maintenance, security and access, signage, and the overall office experience

  • The staffing model (when necessary) for onsite support, including office managers and hourly staff, and the systems that keep each space running without escalation

  • A consistent operating standard so every location runs the same way, as well as playbooks.

  • Space and desk management, access control, and visitor management systems

Team & Budget

  • Eventually, building and leading a small workplace team as the function scales

  • Full ownership of the workplace and real estate budget, capital projects and operating costs

  • Vendor sourcing, contracts, and performance management

Your First 12 Months

  • Get all active office projects under a single plan, budget, and timeline

  • Establish the facilities operating standard and onsite staffing model for our existing locations

  • Build the real estate and workplace playbook so the next office opening is repeatable, not improvised

  • Hire the first members of your workplace team

What You Bring

  • 10+ years in workplace, real estate, facilities, or capital projects, including end-to-end ownership of at least one office buildout

  • Ability to travel. Given the nature of this role, you will have to be available to travel to multiple offices and locations frequently.

  • Direct experience negotiating or managing commercial leases, working with brokers, landlords, and Legal

  • Strong construction and vendor project management — you can hold architects, CMs, and GCs to scope, budget, and schedule

  • Working knowledge of permitting, building codes, accessibility, and workplace safety

  • Experience delivering or operating space used for public events, customer-facing programming, or brand moments

  • Budget ownership for capital and operating spend, with sound commercial judgment

  • Comfort operating with ambiguity in a fast-moving, scaling company — you don't wait for a playbook, you write it

  • An eye for how physical space shapes culture, and genuine care for a consistent experience across every location

  • Experience operating across multiple cities or a distributed, remote-first company

  • Experience supporting spaces used for customer-facing events or brand moments

  • Experience leasing or building in international markets, particularly EMEA or APAC

  • Familiarity with lease administration, space management, or IWMS platforms

  • Experience hiring and managing a small ops or facilities team

What You'll Own

Requirements Scoping & Internal Stakeholder Management

 - Converting the CEO and executive team’s vision into a documented program for each site

 - Gathering requirements across Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Developer Relations, People, IT, Security, and Finance to determine how each space will be used and what it needs to solve for

 - Reconciling competing requests into a single prioritized brief, secure executive approval, and own that brief as the source of truth for architects, general contractors, and all subsequent change decisions

Capacity & Space Planning

 - Occupancy forecasting and space programming against the company headcount plan, in partnership with Finance and People

 - Recommendations on the size, timing, and location of new and expanded space, grounded in utilization data rather than anecdote

 - The tradeoff at each site between event capacity, collaboration space, and focus work, documented and revisited as headcount changes

Real Estate & Leasing

 - Site selection, tours, and location recommendations as we evaluate new and expanded spaces

 - Lease negotiation and renewals, partnering with Finance and Legal on LOIs, term sheets, insurance needs, and commercial terms, including tenant improvement allowances, free rent, escalations, letters of credit and security deposits, restoration and holdover obligations, assignment and sublease rights, and expansion and termination flexibility

 - Analysis of lease versus license, coworking, and short-term venue alternatives in markets where a long-term commitment is not yet warranted

 - International site selection and leasing, including engagement of local counsel and brokers, country-specific code and accessibility standards, and coordination with Finance, People, and Legal on the entity, tax, and employment implications of each location

 - Partnership with Accounting on lease classification and ASC 842 treatment, and delivery of the underlying data Finance needs for budgeting, forecasting, and audit

 - Landlord and broker relationships, and ownership of all real estate documentation and key dates

Construction & Buildout

 - End-to-end project management of office buildouts, from design intent through permitting, construction, and move-in

 - Coordination of architects, general contractors, designers, and trades — holding scope, budget, and timeline

 - Design and delivery of assembly and event space, including occupancy classification and egress, load-in and rigging, AV and streaming infrastructure, acoustics, power and network capacity for large gatherings, and commercial or catered food service

 - Permitting, code, accessibility, and safety compliance across every project

Facilities & Workplace Operations

 - Day-to-day operations across all offices: supplies, maintenance, security and access, signage, and the overall office experience

 - The staffing model (when necessary) for onsite support, including office managers and hourly staff, and the systems that keep each space running without escalation

 - A consistent operating standard so every location runs the same way, as well as playbooks.

 - Space and desk management, access control, and visitor management systems

Team & Budget

 - Eventually, building and leading a small workplace team as the function scales

 - Full ownership of the workplace and real estate budget, capital projects and operating costs

 - Vendor sourcing, contracts, and performance management

Your First 12 Months

 - Get all active office projects under a single plan, budget, and timeline

 - Establish the facilities operating standard and onsite staffing model for our existing locations

 - Build the real estate and workplace playbook so the next office opening is repeatable, not improvised

 - Hire the first members of your workplace team

What You Bring

 - 10+ years in workplace, real estate, facilities, or capital projects, including end-to-end ownership of at least one office buildout

 - Ability to travel. Given the nature of this role, you will have to be available to travel to multiple offices and locations frequently.

 - Direct experience negotiating or managing commercial leases, working with brokers, landlords, and Legal

 - Strong construction and vendor project management — you can hold architects, CMs, and GCs to scope, budget, and schedule

 - Working knowledge of permitting, building codes, accessibility, and workplace safety

 - Experience delivering or operating space used for public events, customer-facing programming, or brand moments

 - Budget ownership for capital and operating spend, with sound commercial judgment

 - Comfort operating with ambiguity in a fast-moving, scaling company — you don't wait for a playbook, you write it

 - An eye for how physical space shapes culture, and genuine care for a consistent experience across every location

 - Experience operating across multiple cities or a distributed, remote-first company

 - Experience supporting spaces used for customer-facing events or brand moments

 - Experience leasing or building in international markets, particularly EMEA or APAC

 - Familiarity with lease administration, space management, or IWMS platforms

 - Experience hiring and managing a small ops or facilities team

jobs.title: Executive Assistant, Marketing
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

Team Overview

You'd be the right hand to our CMO and a force multiplier for the marketing leadership team. Marketing owns how the world discovers what Deepgram can do, and the CMO's time and focus are among the highest-leverage resources we have. Your job is to protect that leverage: keep the operation running cleanly enough that leadership stays heads-down on the work that moves the business, and connect the dots across teams so the right things meet at the right time.

Key Goals

  • Protect and optimize the CMO's calendar — partner with them to set and re-sequence priorities as the picture shifts, so their time lands on strategic work rather than reactive fire drills

  • Run the marketing leadership operating cadence (staff meetings, QBRs, offsites, planning cycles) and coordinate with adjacent teams — RevOps, Comms, People — so cross-functional work lands without the CMO having to chase it

  • Build Human+AI workflows for scheduling, inbox triage, and meeting prep that cut recurring admin turnaround by [X]%

  • Spot recurring friction in how leadership operates and ship [1–2] fixes a quarter — a template, a cadence, an automation — instead of absorbing the same problem every week

  • Own complex travel and logistics with zero missed connections, and close expenses same-day

  • Keep confidential and sensitive matters secure, handling delicate information with total discretion

Minimum Skills, Knowledge & Capabilities

  • Operates AI-native — designs Human+AI workflows for scheduling, drafting, and meeting prep rather than doing every task by hand

  • Builds lightweight systems that eliminate recurring admin work instead of re-solving it each week

  • Identifies problems in how the office runs and proposes practical solutions within the function

  • Coordinates across teams and programs, not just within a single leader's calendar

  • Exercises sound judgment and discretion with confidential and sensitive information

  • Juggles competing priorities across time zones and calendars without dropping details

  • Communicates clearly and professionally with senior stakeholders, internal and external

  • Anticipates needs and resolves problems before they reach the CMO's desk

Preferred Qualifications (nice-to-have, not required)

  • Typically ~1–3 years supporting leaders or coordinating across teams, or equivalent demonstrated experience

  • Prior experience supporting a senior leader or executive, [in a fast-moving startup or high-growth tech environment]

  • Hands-on with modern AI tools for drafting, summarizing, and automating repetitive work

  • Familiarity with common exec-support tooling — [calendar, travel, expense, and comms platforms]

Our Values

  • Be You — bring your whole self and a different perspective; diverse viewpoints make our products better.

  • Be Curious — challenge the status quo, keep learning, and ask 'how might we?' instead of accepting limits.

  • Grow Together — push each other to do great work, treat feedback as a gift, and leave the drama out.

  • Do the Right Thing — act with integrity and candor, assume best intent, choose ethics over expediency.

  • Think Smart. Act Fast. — weigh the high-leverage options, decide, and move; no analysis paralysis.

  • Put the Customer First — listen with empathy, understand their goals, and let their success drive ours.

We know the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting great candidates — so please don't hesitate to apply. We'd love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Accounting Manager, GL& Close
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

We're hiring an Accounting Manager, GL & Close to run the more complex parts of our monthly close and to push large sections of it forward as Deepgram scales through its first external audit and toward public markets. You'll report directly to the Chief Accounting Officer on a small, deliberately lean finance team, and transition to the Senior Director, Accounting once that role is filled — which means unusual proximity to the top of the function from day one, and a manager above you who has taken a company through this exact arc before.

Your manager owns the close. You own the parts of it that carry the most judgment, and you move the rest of it along without waiting to be asked. Practically, that means you'll prepare in the areas where the answer depends on a call rather than a formula, and review in the areas where the process is established — with the line between the two moving as the team grows and as the business gets more complicated.

This is a hands-on role. You'll be in the workpapers, not just over them. If you're looking for a seat where you assign schedules and approve them, this isn't it. If you want to own the technically hardest work in the close while developing the people who own the rest, it is.

It's also a build, not a maintain. The close you inherit is a startup close. The close you leave behind has to survive an external audit, an ERP migration off Xero, and SOX — and it has to run on a team that stays small, which means it runs on AI. We're not looking for someone who closes faster with AI on the side. We're looking for someone who rebuilds the work around it.

What You'll Do

  • Push the close forward. Own the critical-path workstreams and drive them to done. Chase open items, unblock the team, escalate early, and keep the calendar honest. When the close lands on time, it's because you moved it.

  • Prepare the complex and judgmental areas. Stock-based compensation, leases, capitalized software, payroll and compensation accruals, intercompany and foreign currency are examples of where we'd expect your own hands on the schedule — but the list will shift with what the business throws at us. The constant is that the hard ones come to you, and you build them well enough to defend to an auditor.

  • Review the established areas. Fixed assets, prepaids, cash, recurring accruals and journal entries, AP, expense reports — prepared by the Senior Accountant and our offshore team, reviewed by you. Your review is where the quality bar gets set, and it should teach as well as catch. Expect to roll up your sleeves and prepare in these areas too when volume, timing, or complexity calls for it.

  • Own the tie-out and the story. Consolidation and the close package, plus flux — month-over-month and budget-to-actual — in narrative the CAO and CFO can read once and act on.

  • Manage and develop the team. Coach the Senior Accountant, set the standard, and delegate in a way that grows them rather than just moving work off your plate. Hire the next accountant as we scale.

  • Be a day-to-day owner in our first external audit. Build the PBC packages for your areas, run the walkthroughs, and answer the auditors directly.

  • Design close controls that survive SOX. Documented, evidenced, repeatable — built in now, not retrofitted the year before we file.

  • Own your workstream in the ERP migration off Xero. Close-process design, subledger and schedule migration, cutover reconciliations, parallel-run validation.

  • Rebuild the work around AI. Reconciliation matching, anomaly detection, schedule and rollforward generation, first-draft entries and flux narratives, PBC assembly, workflow automation. Build tooling the team runs without you in the room.

What You'll Need

  • 6+ years of progressive accounting experience, including hands-on ownership of technical close areas — things like stock compensation, leases, capitalized software, or payroll accounting — and real experience reviewing another accountant's work.

  • Active CPA preferred. Big 4 or national firm foundation a plus.

  • Deep operational US GAAP fluency where it's hardest. Capitalization judgment, equity compensation, leases, payroll and compensation, intercompany, foreign currency, and cutoff. You know where the judgment lives, not just where the guidance is — and you can build a schedule from a blank page.

  • Hands-on ERP and systems experience. Comfort with equity administration platforms (Carta or similar), payroll systems, close tooling (Numeric, FloQast, BlackLine or similar), and spend platforms (Ramp or similar).

  • A demonstrated AI-native working style. This is a requirement, not a preference. You use LLMs daily on accounting work. You have reasoned, specific views on where AI is trustworthy in a close — reconciliation matching, anomaly detection, schedule generation, first-draft narratives, PBC assembly — and where it isn't: materiality calls, capitalization judgment, cutoff, novel technical positions. And at least one thing you've built is in daily use by people other than you. We run a dedicated interview on this and we don't soften it.

  • Comfort vibe-coding small scripts (Python, SQL, Apps Script) for schedules, reconciliations, data pulls, and automation. A real expectation at this level — Deepgram's AI-native operating model applies to every finance hire, and managers here extend their own work with tooling they build.

  • Reviewer instincts. Review that raises the bar rather than just catching errors, and feedback the other person can actually use.

  • A builder's instinct. Comfort with ambiguity, no waiting for a playbook, strong bias to ship.

  • Strong written communication. You can explain a variance or a technical entry to a non-finance leader without losing them, and write support the auditors don't come back on.

  • High integrity, high ownership, low ego.

It Would Be Great If You Had

  • Experience preparing for or running a company's first external audit.

  • Experience implementing or migrating an ERP — particularly off a small-business system onto a scale platform.

  • SaaS, usage-based, or AI infrastructure accounting experience.

  • Exposure to multi-entity and international intercompany accounting.

  • SOX control design and documentation experience, or a public-company close under your belt.

  • Experience working with an offshore or outsourced accounting team.

  • Reasoned views on the modern accounting stack — NetSuite, Rillet, Numeric, FloQast, Carta, Ramp — developed through use, not through vendor decks.

  • TTS or generative-audio models deployed at meaningful production scale.

  • Sophisticated evaluation systems for generative speech; expressive or multilingual generation, voice cloning and adaptation, or controllable generation.

  • Recognized external contributions — publications, open source, patents, invited talks — in speech synthesis, neural audio codecs, speech language models, or multimodal models.

  • Experience in fast-moving startup or research environments that routinely take models from idea to production.

This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

About the Role

Deepgram is hiring a Director of Brand Strategy & Narrative to own what we say and how we say it. You will define the voice of voice, shaping Deepgram’s brand strategy, narrative, and verbal identity across company positioning, product naming, copy, executive communications, and the arguments we make onstage and in public.

This role requires both strategic leadership and exceptional writing craft. You’ll define the argument for why voice is becoming the preferred interface, establish Deepgram’s role in a voice-first future, and turn that strategy into language people remember and repeat. At the same time, you’ll stay close to the work—writing keynotes, launch narratives, hero pages, manifestos, and other high-impact brand moments yourself.

Reporting to the Head of Brand & Awareness, you’ll lead and develop writing talent while partnering closely with Deepgram’s Design Director and broader creative team in an integrated studio model. You’ll help build the verbal function as Deepgram scales, raising the standard of the work while creating the systems, guidance, and team needed to deliver it consistently.

This is a remote-first role within a fast-moving, category-defining company. Success requires comfort with ambiguity, rapid change, and the pace of AI—as well as the judgment to know when to move quickly and when the work needs to be pushed further.

What You’ll Own

  • Brand strategy and narrative — defining and evolving the argument for why voice is becoming the preferred interface, Deepgram’s role in a voice-first future, and why it matters now.

  • Company and product positioning — building a cohesive positioning strategy that connects the company story to individual products so every expression of the brand strengthens the whole.

  • Category-defining language — translating Deepgram’s technical differentiation and category leadership into clear, memorable language people repeat when we’re not in the room.

  • Brand architecture — defining how the portfolio is organized, what constitutes a platform, product, or feature, and how each offering relates to the others.

  • Naming — leading naming initiatives end to end, from strategy and generation through evaluation, stakeholder alignment, and legal clearance.

  • Verbal identity — establishing Deepgram’s voice, tone, lexicon, and language principles, then building practical guidelines that make the system usable across the company.

  • High-impact writing — personally writing and shaping the work that matters most, including manifestos, launch narratives, hero pages, keynotes, and other flagship brand moments.

  • Executive narratives — partnering closely with founders and senior leaders to shape the arguments Deepgram makes in public and how those ideas are communicated.

  • Thought leadership and content strategy — defining what Deepgram publishes, where it appears, who it serves, and how it advances the company narrative. The work should earn attention through the strength of the thinking, not the volume of output.

  • Writing team leadership — building, mentoring, and growing a high-performing team of writers. You set priorities, give direct feedback, develop talent, and hold the standard for the team’s output.

  • Creative quality — leading copy reviews that strengthen the work and raise the level of craft across internal teams, agencies, freelancers, and contract writers.

  • Cross-functional partnership — working closely with design, web, product, demand generation, developer relations, communications, legal, and other teams to bring the narrative to life consistently.

  • AI-native execution — actively using AI tools in your own writing and strategy work while pushing the team to explore new ways AI can improve creative development, quality, and speed.

What We’re Looking For

  • 10+ years of experience across writing, narrative development, and brand strategy, including at least four years leading people and creative work

  • Exceptional writing ability across formats, from strategic keynotes and manifestos to headlines, product copy, and button labels

  • A portfolio demonstrating brand narrative, positioning, naming, and brand architecture work that shipped

  • Direct experience building portfolio and naming systems, not simply contributing to them

  • A strong creative leader who gets energy from developing writers and raising the quality of a team’s work while remaining an exceptional individual craftsperson

  • Technical fluency and genuine curiosity—you can work with engineers, understand what they built and why it matters, and translate that complexity into something people want to read

  • Experience working in an in-house or agency studio model where writers and designers develop ideas together at speed

  • Executive presence and experience shaping what founders and senior leaders say—and how they say it

  • Strong cross-functional communication skills and the ability to earn support for an idea from writers, engineers, marketers, and executives

  • Excellent creative judgment, with the taste and conviction to articulate why an idea or piece of work is or isn’t working

  • Comfort operating through ambiguity and rapid change in a fast-moving company undergoing significant brand evolution

  • Active use of AI in writing, research, ideation, or creative development—not just interest in what it could eventually do

It Would Be Nice If You Had

  • Experience branding technical, developer-focused, or AI products and making complex technology feel clear and human

  • Experience leading external brand or creative agencies through naming, positioning, or narrative engagements

  • A background in speechwriting, editorial, journalism, or another discipline grounded in rigorous storytelling

Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.

jobs.title: Customer Success Engineer (Scaled)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity

The Scaled Team is how Deepgram delivers world-class customer success to our fastest-growing segment — at scale. Instead of one CSE per account, you'll drive adoption, retention, and expansion across a large, pooled portfolio through a digital-first, one-to-many motion: automated customer journeys, programmatic outreach, self-serve enablement, and well-timed human touchpoints at the moments that matter most.

This is a role for a deeply technical systems builder. You'll be as comfortable troubleshooting an API integration as designing the onboarding sequence, webinar, or automated workflow that helps hundreds of customers hit value faster. Your leverage doesn't come from how many meetings you take — it comes from the repeatable systems you build that make every customer feel like they have a dedicated engineer in their corner.

Who You Are

You're not a traditional CSM. You're a Customer Success Engineer who works at the intersection of APIs, customer outcomes, and scale — credible running demos, guiding integration and architecture decisions, and helping customers get from prototype to production. What sets you apart is the instinct to turn a one-off fix into something scalable: a playbook, an automation, a self-serve resource that solves the same problem for every customer who comes after. You've shipped something — an internal tool, an agent, a script, a pipeline, a customer-facing program — that permanently eliminated a class of problems for you, your team, or your customers.

You're energized by serving a high volume of customers without dropping the quality bar. You ramp quickly on unfamiliar accounts, prioritize ruthlessly through a business-impact lens, and are comfortable working a shared, pooled book rather than a fixed set of named accounts. You have high EQ and a high learning index — you read a customer's situation fast and absorb technical and business complexity faster. You write exceptionally well, because your writing has to scale across hundreds of customers at once. And you question the status quo: the fact that we do something a certain way isn't evidence it's the best way.

AI is how you work, not a tool you reach for occasionally. You've rebuilt a meaningful part of your workflow around it, and going back to the old way would feel like working with one hand tied behind your back. You'd refuse to.

What You'll Do

  • Own adoption, retention, and expansion across a large, pooled portfolio of Scaled-segment customers — through a one-to-many motion, not dedicated 1:1 coverage.

  • Design and execute scalable customer journeys — digital onboarding sequences, automated lifecycle touchpoints, in-app guidance, self-serve resources — that drive fast time-to-first-value and consistent activation.

  • Show up in person at the moments that matter: activation, technical blockers, expansion signals, renewal, and risk.

  • Provide hands-on technical guidance — run and record demos, guide API integrations and architecture decisions, troubleshoot L1/L2 issues — for developer and technical audiences, backed by deep, current knowledge of Deepgram's APIs and how customers build on them.

  • Build and maintain reusable enablement assets (demo scripts, integration guides, sample code, evaluation kits, playbooks, micro-videos) that customers and GTM teams can run without live support.

  • Run one-to-many programs — webinars, office hours, education campaigns — that drive product adoption and surface expansion across the segment.

  • Monitor account health, usage, and churn-risk signals across the portfolio and trigger proactive, prioritized outreach off the data.

  • Identify and scope expansion opportunities (cross-sell, upsell, multi-product) at scale, partnering with Sales on higher-value plays.

  • Serve as the voice of the customer internally, turning digital interactions and usage data into input on product roadmap, GTM strategy, and the internal tools we build.

  • Track, analyze, and report portfolio-level KPIs: activation, adoption, usage, health, retention, expansion.

  • Build the systems that make scaled success compound. If you catch yourself doing something manually more than twice — research, account summaries, follow-ups, content, technical investigation — your next move is to build the thing that removes it. Your output is measured not just by the customers you serve, but by the leverage you create for the whole segment.

It's Important To Us That You Have

  • 3–5+ years in a technical, customer-facing role — Customer Success Engineering, Sales Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Implementation, Technical Account Management, or Support Engineering — at an API-driven, developer-first, or AI company.

  • Fluency in APIs, developer workflows, and integration patterns, enough to run demos and troubleshoot L1/L2 issues. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you must be genuinely credible in technical conversations with developers.

  • Experience serving a high volume of customers or building scaled/tech-touch programs (digital onboarding, one-to-many campaigns, webinars, self-serve enablement, automated journeys).

  • Systems thinking and process orientation — you've built repeatable playbooks, templates, or automations that worked across many customers.

  • A data-driven mindset: comfortable using product usage and customer health data to prioritize, measure, and refine your work.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to create content that educates and drives action across a broad audience.

  • In your application: tell us about something you built — a tool, agent, script, workflow, or customer program — that permanently eliminated recurring work. What it replaced, and what it's still doing today.

  • A strong sense of ownership and comfort working both collaboratively and independently in a remote environment.

It Would Be Great If You Had

  • Experience in a scaled, digital, or tech-touch Customer Success motion, and/or with consumption-based business models.

  • Working fluency with automation, scripting, or agent-building (Python, TypeScript, workflow tools, agent frameworks) — enough to ship working systems.

  • Experience with Customer Success, customer education, or marketing-automation platforms (Gainsight, Vitally, ChurnZero, or similar) and product analytics tools.

  • Experience in AI, ML, voice AI, cloud infrastructure, or developer-first technologies.

  • A background in Customer Education, Scaled/Digital Success, or Customer Marketing alongside technical customer-facing work.

Instead of one CSE per account, you'll drive adoption, retention, and expansion across a large, pooled portfolio through a digital-first, one-to-many motion: automated customer journeys, programmatic outreach, self-serve enablement, and well-timed human touchpoints at the moments that matter most.



This is a role for a deeply technical systems builder. You'll be as comfortable troubleshooting an API integration as designing the onboarding sequence, webinar, or automated workflow that helps hundreds of customers hit value faster. Your leverage doesn't come from how many meetings you take — it comes from the repeatable systems you build that make every customer feel like they have a dedicated engineer in their corner.


WHO YOU ARE

You're not a traditional CSM. You're a Customer Success Engineer who works at the intersection of APIs, customer outcomes, and scale — credible running demos, guiding integration and architecture decisions, and helping customers get from prototype to production. What sets you apart is the instinct to turn a one-off fix into something scalable: a playbook, an automation, a self-serve resource that solves the same problem for every customer who comes after. You've shipped something — an internal tool, an agent, a script, a pipeline, a customer-facing program — that permanently eliminated a class of problems for you, your team, or your customers.



You're energized by serving a high volume of customers without dropping the quality bar. You ramp quickly on unfamiliar accounts, prioritize ruthlessly through a business-impact lens, and are comfortable working a shared, pooled book rather than a fixed set of named accounts. You have high EQ and a high learning index — you read a customer's situation fast and absorb technical and business complexity faster. You write exceptionally well, because your writing has to scale across hundreds of customers at once. And you question the status quo: the fact that we do something a certain way isn't evidence it's the best way.



AI is how you work, not a tool you reach for occasionally. You've rebuilt a meaningful part of your workflow around it, and going back to the old way would feel like working with one hand tied behind your back. You'd refuse to.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own adoption, retention, and expansion across a large, pooled portfolio of Scaled-segment customers — through a one-to-many motion, not dedicated 1:1 coverage.

 - Design and execute scalable customer journeys — digital onboarding sequences, automated lifecycle touchpoints, in-app guidance, self-serve resources — that drive fast time-to-first-value and consistent activation.

 - Show up in person at the moments that matter: activation, technical blockers, expansion signals, renewal, and risk.

 - Provide hands-on technical guidance — run and record demos, guide API integrations and architecture decisions, troubleshoot L1/L2 issues — for developer and technical audiences, backed by deep, current knowledge of Deepgram's APIs and how customers build on them.

 - Build and maintain reusable enablement assets (demo scripts, integration guides, sample code, evaluation kits, playbooks, micro-videos) that customers and GTM teams can run without live support.

 - Run one-to-many programs — webinars, office hours, education campaigns — that drive product adoption and surface expansion across the segment.

 - Monitor account health, usage, and churn-risk signals across the portfolio and trigger proactive, prioritized outreach off the data.

 - Identify and scope expansion opportunities (cross-sell, upsell, multi-product) at scale, partnering with Sales on higher-value plays.

 - Serve as the voice of the customer internally, turning digital interactions and usage data into input on product roadmap, GTM strategy, and the internal tools we build.

 - Track, analyze, and report portfolio-level KPIs: activation, adoption, usage, health, retention, expansion.

 - Build the systems that make scaled success compound. If you catch yourself doing something manually more than twice — research, account summaries, follow-ups, content, technical investigation — your next move is to build the thing that removes it. Your output is measured not just by the customers you serve, but by the leverage you create for the whole segment.


IT'S IMPORTANT TO US THAT YOU HAVE

 - 3–5+ years in a technical, customer-facing role — Customer Success Engineering, Sales Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Implementation, Technical Account Management, or Support Engineering — at an API-driven, developer-first, or AI company.

 - Fluency in APIs, developer workflows, and integration patterns, enough to run demos and troubleshoot L1/L2 issues. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you must be genuinely credible in technical conversations with developers.

 - Experience serving a high volume of customers or building scaled/tech-touch programs (digital onboarding, one-to-many campaigns, webinars, self-serve enablement, automated journeys).

 - Systems thinking and process orientation — you've built repeatable playbooks, templates, or automations that worked across many customers.

 - A data-driven mindset: comfortable using product usage and customer health data to prioritize, measure, and refine your work.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to create content that educates and drives action across a broad audience.

 - In your application: tell us about something you built — a tool, agent, script, workflow, or customer program — that permanently eliminated recurring work. What it replaced, and what it's still doing today.

 - A strong sense of ownership and comfort working both collaboratively and independently in a remote environment.


IT WOULD BE GREAT IF YOU HAD

 - Experience in a scaled, digital, or tech-touch Customer Success motion, and/or with consumption-based business models.

 - Working fluency with automation, scripting, or agent-building (Python, TypeScript, workflow tools, agent frameworks) — enough to ship working systems.

 - Experience with Customer Success, customer education, or marketing-automation platforms (Gainsight, Vitally, ChurnZero, or similar) and product analytics tools.

 - Experience in AI, ML, voice AI, cloud infrastructure, or developer-first technologies.

 - A background in Customer Education, Scaled/Digital Success, or Customer Marketing alongside technical customer-facing work.

jobs.title: Revenue Accounting Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity

We’re hiring a Revenue Accounting Manager to own the revenue close and the monthly application of ASC 606 as Deepgram scales through its first external audit. You’ll report to the Director, Revenue Accounting and manage our revenue accountant.

Customers commit to a dollar amount up front, usually over a twelve to twenty-four month term, and draw it down on API usage. Alongside that we run a self-serve consumption business, plus arrangements involving credits, overage, trained models, concurrency, and more.

We’re working through our 606 positions now, which means the person in this seat helps shape them rather than inheriting them. We’re looking for someone who can carry a position from the guidance through to a schedule an auditor can test, a process that holds up every month once volume inevitably doubles, and an explanation other teams can follow when they want to know why we’re asking. Plenty of people have depth in one of those, but fewer carry all three end to end. You’ll own the close and the schedules underneath it, and build the rest alongside the Director, Revenue Accounting and the Director, Technical Accounting. Controls get designed in partnership rather than handed down, and because the process, reporting, and automation we need are mid-flight, you’ll spend real time with CS, Sales, and Engineering.

The person who does well here would rather build the schedule than take one as given, and stays curious about what’s happening in the business behind the number, because the answer usually comes from a conversation with Sales, CS, or Engineering rather than from the ledger.

What You'll Do

Run the monthly revenue close. Enterprise committed usage, self-serve consumption, and direct entries, reconciled and tied out on the same date every month. Self-serve comes in through the payments stack, and building that into the close cleanly is part of the work.

Own contract liability and deferred revenue. By customer and by contract, tying to the GL and rebuildable from source rather than rolled forward on faith.

Apply the 606 policy suite every month. Material rights on credit rollover, breakage on unused commitments, standalone selling price and discount allocation across platform usage, support, trained models, and concurrency, and contract modifications on upsells, renewals, and co-terms. You’ll build the analysis and the schedules the technical positions rest on, working through them with the Directors as the positions get set.

Explain what moved and why. Monthly and quarterly flux on revenue and deferred revenue, the metrics that come out of the close, and the analysis behind them. This is what the executive team and the board see when they ask how revenue is tracking, what Deal Desk and CS come back to when a deal doesn’t look the way they expected, and what auditors test against.

Be a real manager to our revenue accountant. You’re their first call when something doesn’t tie, and the person who makes sure they’re getting better at the work rather than just getting through it. That relationship is also the backbone of a preparer and reviewer split with segregation of duties and a management review control an auditor can test.

Own the usage-to-billing-to-GL reconciliation. Write the accounting spec that says what has to tie, at what grain, within what tolerance, and what happens when it doesn’t, then hold the tooling Engineering builds to it. The goal is fewer exceptions to work by hand, not more hands to work them.

Be the auditors’ day-to-day contact on revenue, and build the controls that outlast the audit. PBC packages, walkthroughs, and the back and forth on your areas. Then the control design that comes out of it, built with the Directors, starting from the revenue assertions and working back to owner, frequency, and evidence, designed now so there’s enough operating history to rely on when SOX arrives.

Get involved before the ink dries. Deal Desk, Sales, CS, and Legal on order form terms, credits, and overage mechanics. The cheapest revenue problem to fix is the one caught before signature.

Take the revenue workstream in the platform migration. Requirements from the revenue side, close process design, data migration and cutover reconciliations, parallel run validation, built alongside the Director, Revenue Accounting. You’d be joining while this is live.

Rebuild the close around AI. Term extraction and classification, reconciliation matching, anomaly detection, schedule and rollforward generation, first-draft variance narratives, PBC assembly. Build tooling the team runs without you in the room.

What You'll Need

Seven or more years in accounting with most of it in revenue, including owning a monthly or quarterly close start to finish and reviewing another accountant’s work.

You make the person you manage better. Review that raises the bar rather than just catching errors, and feedback someone can act on. We care about people getting better here, which applies to the accountant you’ll manage and to you, since this is a function that will keep growing and the person building it grows with it.

Hands-on ASC 606 in a consumption or drawdown model. Prepaid commitments burned down over a term, credits, overage, and the balance left at renewal. We’ve weighted this heavily because almost none of it looks like ratable subscription work, and you’d be applying it in your first month.

Depth in the topics that will define our audit. Material rights, breakage and forfeiture estimation, standalone selling price and allocation, variable consideration, contract modifications, contract liabilities, and gross versus net. Enough that you could build the position and the schedule from a blank page.

You can do the data work yourself. SQL, Python, or a spreadsheet methodology you can walk someone through end to end, including how you’d handle an unmatched residual and what tolerance you’d accept. A lot of what you’ll reconcile lives in systems that don’t share a key.

A working AI practice. You use LLMs on revenue work regularly, and you’ve got views on where they’re trustworthy in a close, term extraction, reconciliation matching, anomaly flagging, schedule generation, first drafts, and where they aren’t, the material right conclusion, the breakage estimate, the modification call. Ideally at least one thing you’ve built is being used by someone other than you.

Systems fluency. A billing and revenue platform such as Ordway, Zuora, Maxio, RevPro, NetSuite ARM, or Rillet, a payments stack, a CRM, and a GL, with views you formed through using them rather than from vendor decks.

You write clearly for people who don’t do this work. Explaining why revenue moved to someone outside accounting, and writing a position an auditor doesn’t come back on.

Active CPA preferred, and a Big 4 or national firm foundation is a plus.

High integrity, high ownership, low ego.

It Would Be Great If You Had

Experience preparing for or running a company’s first external audit, on the revenue accounts specifically.

Experience standing up revenue controls, whether that’s a RACM through to ICFR or SOX revenue cycles at a newly public company.

Experience implementing or migrating a billing and revenue platform.

Both an enterprise and a self-serve revenue motion under one roof.

A breakage or forfeiture estimate you built from scratch, including sourcing the historical data behind it.

AI infrastructure, developer platform, or API-metered revenue experience.

Exposure to multi-entity or international revenue and the related intercompany mechanics.

jobs.title: Forward-Deployed Engineer (FDE), Strategic Accounts
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity

Most engineering roles ask you to build the platform. This one asks you to build everything between the platform and a customer's success: the solutions, integrations, and tooling that run in production for some of the largest enterprises in the world.

Deepgram is seeking Forward-Deployed Engineers for our strategic accounts. You'll embed with one strategic customer at a time, working directly with their technical and business teams, alongside Deepgram's core research teams. Today's engagements center on leading restaurant enterprises and restaurant technology partners (we already partner with several of the world's leading restaurant brands), and the examples in this posting come from that work.

As a Forward-Deployed Engineer, you'll take Deepgram's voice AI platform the last mile. That means production-scale integrations with the systems that your customer actually runs on (today, that's point of sale, loyalty, payment gateways, and customer data platforms), voice agents that take live orders from customers every day, and everything in between: the tooling, prompt engineering, and evaluation work that bridges what Deepgram offers today and what makes your customer successful tomorrow.

Forward-deployed means you do this work with your customer, not just for them. You'll be on site regularly, embedded with their technical team, and close enough to the business to see problems before they become escalations. You'll also have a senior Forward-Deployed Engineer alongside you, reviewing your work before it ships and bringing you into customer meetings. And the platform is not a fixed product that you implement. When your customer needs a capability that the platform does not offer yet, you'll be the one who proves what it should do next, and what you build and learn in the field becomes part of Deepgram's offering for every customer after yours.

About Forward-Deployed Engineering at Deepgram

Forward-Deployed Engineering is how Deepgram embeds with its most strategic accounts. You'll fully deploy into a dedicated account pod (a small, cross-functional team built around one strategic customer) for a defined stretch, working inside of that account's day to day with a high degree of autonomy. Full deployment means exactly that: while you're deployed, your pod's account is your only customer assignment, with no time split across other accounts or teams. Your work directly shapes how some of the world's largest brands put voice AI in front of their customers.

Forward-Deployed Engineers are part of our broader Applied Engineering team, which serves as the technical interface between Deepgram and our customers across their entire journey (it combines what other companies split into Forward-Deployed Engineering, Sales Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Implementation, and Technical Support). Applied Engineering is your home team and your growth path. You'll be hired into the Applied Engineer position, which has a single growth ladder from Associate through Principal, and you'll grow proficient across multiple roles over time. The pod is where you're deployed; Applied Engineering is where you grow.

What You'll Do

  • Build and ship whatever the solution needs, whether that's an end-to-end service, an integration, internal tooling, or agent and prompt engineering

  • Design, develop, and maintain production-scale integrations with the third-party systems that your customer runs on (in today's pods: point of sale, loyalty, payment gateways, customer data platforms)

  • Spend regular time on site with your customer, working directly with their technical and business teams

  • Monitor, debug, and optimize what you ship in production, including some of the hardest audio environments in voice AI (noisy, multi-mic, drive-thru)

  • Work with our research and product teams to push the platform where your customer needs it to go, and feed what you learn in the field back into the product

  • Test changes against live production data and measure whether they move accuracy, latency, and throughput

Time Allocation

  • Embedded customer delivery (60-80%) — Deployments, integrations, and technical problem-solving with your account, plus turning what the field teaches you into reusable solutions, automation, and documentation. Where you sit in that range depends on where your engagement is in its cycle.

  • Scoping and expansion support (10-25%) — Joining detailed solution scoping, shaping statements of work so that what gets promised can be built, and surfacing the expansion opportunities that you spot from inside of the account. Discovery and demos belong to a pre-sales Applied Engineer in your pod; you'll take parts of that work when the account needs it and hand it back when delivery peaks.

  • Internal collaboration (~15%) — Product feedback, knowledge sharing, and contributing to Applied Engineering strategy.

The delivery and scoping buckets trade against each other: at the peak of an engagement, delivery takes the scoping share.

The On-Site Expectation

You'll have regular, recurring time with your customer, and you'll be on site at least once or twice a month. On some accounts, and at the peaks of an engagement (a launch, a critical integration, a high-stakes pilot), on-site time can rise to as much as 80%. Between those stretches, most of your time goes to making the solution succeed: building, integrating, debugging, and shipping.

Your First 90 Days

  • First 30 Days — Complete the accelerated Forward-Deployed onboarding in your first two weeks, covering Deepgram's technology, products, competitive landscape, and core APIs. The standard Applied Engineer ramp runs four to six weeks. Yours is faster because your pod is waiting. Then spend the back half of the month in motion:

    • Shadow your pod's active engagement

    • Make your first customer site visit alongside a senior Forward-Deployed Engineer

    • Take ownership of your first workstream (an integration, a tool, or a production issue), with your work reviewed before it ships

  • 60 Days — Own a meaningful slice of your customer's solution:

    • Join the on-site rhythm and build relationships with your customer's technical team

    • Ship work that runs in production

  • 90 Days — Operate with independence:

    • Run your own on-site visits and own your slice end to end

    • Bring what the field teaches you back to the team as product feedback and reusable building blocks

    • Join your first solution-scoping conversations with the pod

You'll Love This Role If You

  • See yourself as an engineer first who happens to be great with customers, not the other way around

  • Thrive in high-ambiguity environments where moving fast and making sound decisions under pressure are part of the job

  • Enjoy embedding deeply with customers, building trust, and becoming their go-to technical partner

  • Find satisfaction in shipping production systems and watching them run in the physical world (a drive-thru at rush hour is an honest test environment)

  • Want to grow quickly, with high-stakes accounts, a steep learning curve, and a senior engineer reviewing your work

What We Look For

The software bar comes first. It's important to us that you have:

  • A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or a record of building that speaks for itself

  • Hands-on experience developing and deploying backend systems that run in production, whether through internships, co-ops, your first years in industry, or projects that shipped to live users

  • Experience with cloud-based infrastructure and API design

  • The instinct to proactively recognize problems and to care about the impact of your work

And because you'll be in the room with customers, we look for the raw materials of customer-facing craft:

  • Relationship building — You genuinely enjoy getting to know the people that you work with, and you invest in those relationships beyond what the immediate task requires.

  • Reading the room — You notice who in a meeting is engaged, who is skeptical, and what is going unsaid.

  • Acting on what you notice — When you spot an opening, whether a stakeholder with a problem that you can solve or a question behind the question, you move on it.

  • Coachability — Nobody arrives with all of this polished. We'll teach the craft. We look for the appetite to learn it and openness to feedback along the way.

It Would Be Great if You Had

  • Experience working with audio or voice interfaces
