There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.




COMPANY OPERATING RHYTHM

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.




THE OPPORTUNITY

Most engineering roles ask you to build the platform. This one asks you to build everything between the platform and a customer's success: the solutions, integrations, and tooling that run in production for some of the largest enterprises in the world.

Deepgram is seeking Forward-Deployed Engineers for our strategic accounts. You'll embed with one strategic customer at a time, working directly with their technical and business teams, alongside Deepgram's core research teams. Today's engagements center on leading restaurant enterprises and restaurant technology partners (we already partner with several of the world's leading restaurant brands), and the examples in this posting come from that work.

As a Forward-Deployed Engineer, you'll take Deepgram's voice AI platform the last mile. That means production-scale integrations with the systems that your customer actually runs on (today, that's point of sale, loyalty, payment gateways, and customer data platforms), voice agents that take live orders from customers every day, and everything in between: the tooling, prompt engineering, and evaluation work that bridges what Deepgram offers today and what makes your customer successful tomorrow.

Forward-deployed means you do this work with your customer, not just for them. You'll be on site regularly, embedded with their technical team, and close enough to the business to see problems before they become escalations. You'll also have a senior Forward-Deployed Engineer alongside you, reviewing your work before it ships and bringing you into customer meetings. And the platform is not a fixed product that you implement. When your customer needs a capability that the platform does not offer yet, you'll be the one who proves what it should do next, and what you build and learn in the field becomes part of Deepgram's offering for every customer after yours.




ABOUT FORWARD-DEPLOYED ENGINEERING AT DEEPGRAM

Forward-Deployed Engineering is how Deepgram embeds with its most strategic accounts. You'll fully deploy into a dedicated account pod (a small, cross-functional team built around one strategic customer) for a defined stretch, working inside of that account's day to day with a high degree of autonomy. Full deployment means exactly that: while you're deployed, your pod's account is your only customer assignment, with no time split across other accounts or teams. Your work directly shapes how some of the world's largest brands put voice AI in front of their customers.

Forward-Deployed Engineers are part of our broader Applied Engineering team, which serves as the technical interface between Deepgram and our customers across their entire journey (it combines what other companies split into Forward-Deployed Engineering, Sales Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Implementation, and Technical Support). Applied Engineering is your home team and your growth path. You'll be hired into the Applied Engineer position, which has a single growth ladder from Associate through Principal, and you'll grow proficient across multiple roles over time. The pod is where you're deployed; Applied Engineering is where you grow.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and ship whatever the solution needs, whether that's an end-to-end service, an integration, internal tooling, or agent and prompt engineering

 - Design, develop, and maintain production-scale integrations with the third-party systems that your customer runs on (in today's pods: point of sale, loyalty, payment gateways, customer data platforms)

 - Spend regular time on site with your customer, working directly with their technical and business teams

 - Monitor, debug, and optimize what you ship in production, including some of the hardest audio environments in voice AI (noisy, multi-mic, drive-thru)

 - Work with our research and product teams to push the platform where your customer needs it to go, and feed what you learn in the field back into the product

 - Test changes against live production data and measure whether they move accuracy, latency, and throughput


TIME ALLOCATION

 - Embedded customer delivery (60-80%) — Deployments, integrations, and technical problem-solving with your account, plus turning what the field teaches you into reusable solutions, automation, and documentation. Where you sit in that range depends on where your engagement is in its cycle.

 - Scoping and expansion support (10-25%) — Joining detailed solution scoping, shaping statements of work so that what gets promised can be built, and surfacing the expansion opportunities that you spot from inside of the account. Discovery and demos belong to a pre-sales Applied Engineer in your pod; you'll take parts of that work when the account needs it and hand it back when delivery peaks.

 - Internal collaboration (~15%) — Product feedback, knowledge sharing, and contributing to Applied Engineering strategy.

The delivery and scoping buckets trade against each other: at the peak of an engagement, delivery takes the scoping share.




THE ON-SITE EXPECTATION

You'll have regular, recurring time with your customer, and you'll be on site at least once or twice a month. On some accounts, and at the peaks of an engagement (a launch, a critical integration, a high-stakes pilot), on-site time can rise to as much as 80%. Between those stretches, most of your time goes to making the solution succeed: building, integrating, debugging, and shipping.




YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

 - First 30 Days — Complete the accelerated Forward-Deployed onboarding in your first two weeks, covering Deepgram's technology, products, competitive landscape, and core APIs. The standard Applied Engineer ramp runs four to six weeks. Yours is faster because your pod is waiting. Then spend the back half of the month in motion:
   
   - Shadow your pod's active engagement
   
   - Make your first customer site visit alongside a senior Forward-Deployed Engineer
   
   - Take ownership of your first workstream (an integration, a tool, or a production issue), with your work reviewed before it ships

 - 60 Days — Own a meaningful slice of your customer's solution:
   
   - Join the on-site rhythm and build relationships with your customer's technical team
   
   - Ship work that runs in production

 - 90 Days — Operate with independence:
   
   - Run your own on-site visits and own your slice end to end
   
   - Bring what the field teaches you back to the team as product feedback and reusable building blocks
   
   - Join your first solution-scoping conversations with the pod


YOU'LL LOVE THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - See yourself as an engineer first who happens to be great with customers, not the other way around

 - Thrive in high-ambiguity environments where moving fast and making sound decisions under pressure are part of the job

 - Enjoy embedding deeply with customers, building trust, and becoming their go-to technical partner

 - Find satisfaction in shipping production systems and watching them run in the physical world (a drive-thru at rush hour is an honest test environment)

 - Want to grow quickly, with high-stakes accounts, a steep learning curve, and a senior engineer reviewing your work


WHAT WE LOOK FOR

The software bar comes first. It's important to us that you have:

 - A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or a record of building that speaks for itself

 - Hands-on experience developing and deploying backend systems that run in production, whether through internships, co-ops, your first years in industry, or projects that shipped to live users

 - Experience with cloud-based infrastructure and API design

 - The instinct to proactively recognize problems and to care about the impact of your work

And because you'll be in the room with customers, we look for the raw materials of customer-facing craft:

 - Relationship building — You genuinely enjoy getting to know the people that you work with, and you invest in those relationships beyond what the immediate task requires.

 - Reading the room — You notice who in a meeting is engaged, who is skeptical, and what is going unsaid.

 - Acting on what you notice — When you spot an opening, whether a stakeholder with a problem that you can solve or a question behind the question, you move on it.

 - Coachability — Nobody arrives with all of this polished. We'll teach the craft. We look for the appetite to learn it and openness to feedback along the way.


IT WOULD BE GREAT IF YOU HAD

 - Experience working with audio or voice interfaces

 - Experience building and maintaining a system that integrates with many third-party APIs, particularly point-of-sale systems

 - Experience taking a system from zero to one

 - Depth in one or more modern languages (our field work spans Python, JavaScript and TypeScript, Rust, Go, Kotlin, and whatever your customer runs), and the flexibility to pick up the next one

 - Experience with containerization tools, such as Docker and Kubernetes

 - Any experience being the technical person in front of a non-technical audience (teaching, tutoring, demos, hackathons, support)

jobs.descriptionHtml:

Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

WHO YOU ARE

You are a full-cycle Account Executive who builds your own pipeline and closes it. You are comfortable selling a product with real technical depth, holding your own with engineers, architects, and technical decision-makers, and translating what the product does into clear business value. You know how to land a new logo and grow it, and you are as comfortable working a partner co-sell as you are running a direct deal.

You are at ease operating across the varied markets and cultures of APAC, and you do your best work in a build environment where the playbook is still forming, priorities move quickly, and your input shapes how the team sells. You are organized, self-directed, and relentless about following up.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own a territory end to end: generate pipeline, run full-cycle deals, and carry a new-business and expansion number.

  • Build your own pipeline through self-prospecting, and work with SDRs and Marketing to grow pipeline and build Deepgram's presence in the market, including representing Deepgram at key developer and industry events.

  • Run both motions, with an emphasis on co-sell: work closely with the technology partners headquartered in Singapore, and sell directly into accounts across the region.

  • Sell across the full spectrum of the market, from fast-moving tech companies to large enterprises, focused on APAC and the broader ANZ region.

  • Land new logos and expand them over time, growing accounts through adoption and new use cases.

  • Work closely with Field Engineers to guide technical evaluations and move customers from evaluation into production.

  • Develop a strong command of customer needs, the competitive landscape, and Deepgram's products, and articulate the value clearly to technical audiences.

  • Maintain accurate pipeline hygiene and forecasting.

  • Bring the voice of the customer back to Deepgram, feeding product feedback and market insight to the team.

 

YOU'LL LOVE THIS ROLE IF YOU

  • Are energized by building early and want to help shape how Deepgram sells across APAC/ANZ.

  • Take pride in building your own pipeline and owning a deal from first touch to close.

  • Are at home selling to technical buyers and can hold your own on the substance of the product.

  • Enjoy running a partner co-sell motion alongside direct selling.

  • Think in terms of landing a logo and growing it, not just closing once.

  • Are passionate about Deepgram's mission and what voice AI makes possible.

 

IT'S IMPORTANT TO US THAT YOU HAVE

  • A track record as a full-cycle Account Executive: building pipeline from scratch, running technical deals, and consistently overachieving against target. We expect this typically means 5 or more years of quota-carrying experience, but we hire at varying levels of seniority and encourage strong candidates to apply.

  • Experience selling products with real technical depth, such as APIs, developer tools, or platforms evaluated on their merits by engineering buyers.

  • Experience selling across APAC/ANZ markets, to both technical and business buyers.

  • Comfort running both a direct motion and a partner or co-sell motion, and strong instincts for working through partners.

  • A land-and-expand mindset, with a history of growing accounts after the initial win.

  • Strong communication and follow-up, and the discipline to run a consistent, repeatable sales process.

  • A history of stable tenure and clear progression across your roles.

 

IT WOULD BE GREAT IF YOU HAD

  • Experience selling voice AI, speech, AI/ML, developer tools, or infrastructure.

  • Experience co-selling through systems integrators or hyperscaler partners.

  • Familiarity with a modern sales methodology such as Challenger.

  • Experience in a high-growth or early-stage environment.

If the idea of building Deepgram's business in APAC/ANZ excites you, we'd like to hear from you.

 

BENEFITS & PERKS

We offer best-in-class benefits, localized to your market. This includes comprehensive health coverage, generous paid time off, paid parental leave, meaningful learning and development support, and stipends to help you do your best work. Specific benefits are administered locally and governed by country-specific regulations.

Backed by prominent investors including Y Combinator, Madrona, Tiger Global, Wing VC and NVIDIA, Deepgram has raised over $215M in total funding. If you're looking to work on cutting-edge technology and make a significant impact in the AI industry, we'd love to hear from you!

Deepgram is an equal opportunity employer. We want all voices and perspectives represented in our workforce. We are a curious bunch focused on collaboration and doing the right thing. We put our customers first, grow together and move quickly. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, pregnancy, parental status, genetic information, political affiliation, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate. We are happy to provide accommodations for applicants who need them.

Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.

jobs.title: Partner Success Engineer (AWS)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

About the team

Our Customer Success team — The Heartbeat of Deepgram — sits at the intersection of partners, product, and growth. We don't just "manage accounts." We make Deepgram succeed inside our partners' environments by combining deep technical expertise, commercial instinct, and an AI-native way of working — and by building the systems that make the whole team's work compound over time.

About this role

This is not a portfolio role. You will own one relationship: AWS.

Deepgram's AWS partnership is our marquee alliance, and it has outgrown shared coverage. You'd inherit a $15M portfolio from day one and become the single accountable owner of it — the person AWS calls, the person who decides, and the person whose problem it is when something goes wrong.

The motion is ISV-on-cloud: Marketplace listings and private offers, co-sell with AWS field teams, joint GTM, consumption growth and commit drawdown. You'll work across AWS's Partner Development Managers, Solutions Architects and account teams to reach end customers, while working internally across our Sales, Product, and Engineering orgs.

If you've been the technical resource on a partner relationship while someone else owned the commercial outcome, this is a step up rather than a lateral — and we'll be looking for evidence you're ready for it.

Who you are

You operate at the intersection of three competencies, and you're genuinely strong across all three.

1. Strategic partner ownership. You have been the accountable owner of a strategic relationship — not a supporting resource on one. You've set the plan rather than executed someone else's, been the escalation point rather than the escalation path, and carried responsibility for retention and growth. You can name what you were authorized to decide without asking permission.

2. Technical consulting. You run demos, guide architecture discussions, troubleshoot integrations, and help partners deploy AI-driven solutions. No coding required, but you're fluent in APIs, developer workflows, and real technical conversations — genuinely conversant, not hand-waving.

3. An AI-native operating model. AI is how you work, not a tool you occasionally reach for. When you hit recurring work, your instinct is to build the system that removes it.

You may have been a Partner Development Manager, Alliances or Channel lead, Partner Success Manager, Technical Account Manager, Partner Solutions Architect, Strategic Account Manager, or a Customer Success leader who built the partner function yourself. We care about the shape of the ownership, not the title on it. Some of the strongest people in this role came from smaller companies where they built the partner motion from scratch.

You thrive on bringing definition to ambiguity. You form a point of view and bring a recommendation rather than staying in open-ended discovery. You're comfortable operating outside your comfort zone, you question the status quo, and you learn fast.

What you'll do

  • Own the AWS relationship end to end — technical adoption, commercial outcomes, retention, and expansion. There is no separate business counterpart; this seat holds both.

  • Be the trusted advisor across AWS stakeholders, from solutions architects and partner development managers up to senior technical and commercial leadership.

  • Drive joint adoption through live demos, workshops, architecture guidance, and troubleshooting — making Deepgram successful inside AWS's environment and in front of their customers.

  • Run the Marketplace and co-sell motion: listings, private offers, deal structuring, commit drawdown, and joint pipeline with AWS field teams.

  • Navigate three-way dynamics where Deepgram, AWS, and the end customer want different things — and find the path that works for all of them.

  • Run partner business reviews and joint planning independently, and identify and scope expansion in partnership with Sales.

  • Act as the voice of the partner internally, influencing roadmap, GTM strategy, and the tools we build.

  • Track adoption, usage, health and expansion to drive outcomes. Travel to partner sites roughly 3–5 times per quarter.

  • Operate AI-first by default, and build tools, agents, and workflows that eliminate recurring work for you and the team. Your impact is measured by the leverage you create, not only the partner you serve.

What we're looking for

  • You have personally owned a strategic partner or customer relationship. Not supported one. You can describe what you decided, what you were accountable for, and what happened when it went badly.

  • Meaningful scale. Accounts or partner books at roughly $500K+ ARR each, or a partner relationship with comparable revenue attached. We want people who have handled real business-value partnerships at a strategic level.

  • Significant experience in technical, customer-facing roles at API-driven, developer-first, cloud, infrastructure, or AI companies. For most people that's roughly 7+ years, but we care more about the shape of your experience than the number.

  • Understanding of partner ecosystems and channel business models — resale, referral, integrations, marketplace, co-marketing, co-selling — and multi-party commercial dynamics.

  • Hands-on experience running demos, POCs, or technical workshops with enterprise partners or customers. Leading them, not attending them.

  • A track record of identifying and landing expansion in complex partner or enterprise relationships — opportunities you found, not ones handed to you.

  • Fluency discussing APIs, integrations, and developer workflows, and troubleshooting L1-style issues.

  • Experience engaging both technical stakeholders and executive buyers.

  • Exceptional communication and influence — concise and structured, across technical and business audiences.

  • Something you've built — a tool, agent, script, or workflow — that permanently eliminated recurring work. In your application, tell us what it was, what it replaced, and what it's still doing today.

  • An AI-native operating model: specific workflows that structurally depend on AI, and a clear account of how you'd rebuild them if those tools disappeared tomorrow.

Nice to have

  • Direct experience with the AWS ecosystem — Marketplace, private offers, CPPO, APN programs, MAP or other funding mechanisms, or co-sell with AWS field teams. This is a strong plus, not a requirement. We'd rather have a proven partner owner who learns AWS than an AWS specialist who has never owned an outcome.

  • Experience with consumption-based commercial models and how technical adoption converts to revenue.

  • Background in machine learning, voice AI, cloud infrastructure, GenAI/GPU workloads, or developer-first technologies.

  • Experience building a partner function from scratch at a smaller company.

  • Working fluency with automation, scripting, or agent-building (Python, TypeScript, workflow tools, agent frameworks, or equivalent). You don't need to be a software engineer — just dangerous enough to ship working systems.

Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.




COMPANY OPERATING RHYTHM

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.




ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Customer Success team — The Heartbeat of Deepgram — sits at the intersection of partners, product, and growth. We don't just "manage accounts." We make Deepgram succeed inside our partners' environments by combining deep technical expertise, commercial instinct, and an AI-native way of working — and by building the systems that make the whole team's work compound over time.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

This is not a portfolio role. You will own one relationship: AWS.

Deepgram's AWS partnership is our marquee alliance, and it has outgrown shared coverage. You'd inherit a $15M portfolio from day one and become the single accountable owner of it — the person AWS calls, the person who decides, and the person whose problem it is when something goes wrong.

The motion is ISV-on-cloud: Marketplace listings and private offers, co-sell with AWS field teams, joint GTM, consumption growth and commit drawdown. You'll work across AWS's Partner Development Managers, Solutions Architects and account teams to reach end customers, while working internally across our Sales, Product, and Engineering orgs.

If you've been the technical resource on a partner relationship while someone else owned the commercial outcome, this is a step up rather than a lateral — and we'll be looking for evidence you're ready for it.




WHO YOU ARE

You operate at the intersection of three competencies, and you're genuinely strong across all three.

1. Strategic partner ownership. You have been the accountable owner of a strategic relationship — not a supporting resource on one. You've set the plan rather than executed someone else's, been the escalation point rather than the escalation path, and carried responsibility for retention and growth. You can name what you were authorized to decide without asking permission.

2. Technical consulting. You run demos, guide architecture discussions, troubleshoot integrations, and help partners deploy AI-driven solutions. No coding required, but you're fluent in APIs, developer workflows, and real technical conversations — genuinely conversant, not hand-waving.

3. An AI-native operating model. AI is how you work, not a tool you occasionally reach for. When you hit recurring work, your instinct is to build the system that removes it.



You may have been a Partner Development Manager, Alliances or Channel lead, Partner Success Manager, Technical Account Manager, Partner Solutions Architect, Strategic Account Manager, or a Customer Success leader who built the partner function yourself. We care about the shape of the ownership, not the title on it. Some of the strongest people in this role came from smaller companies where they built the partner motion from scratch.



You thrive on bringing definition to ambiguity. You form a point of view and bring a recommendation rather than staying in open-ended discovery. You're comfortable operating outside your comfort zone, you question the status quo, and you learn fast.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the AWS relationship end to end — technical adoption, commercial outcomes, retention, and expansion. There is no separate business counterpart; this seat holds both.

 - Be the trusted advisor across AWS stakeholders, from solutions architects and partner development managers up to senior technical and commercial leadership.

 - Drive joint adoption through live demos, workshops, architecture guidance, and troubleshooting — making Deepgram successful inside AWS's environment and in front of their customers.

 - Run the Marketplace and co-sell motion: listings, private offers, deal structuring, commit drawdown, and joint pipeline with AWS field teams.

 - Navigate three-way dynamics where Deepgram, AWS, and the end customer want different things — and find the path that works for all of them.

 - Run partner business reviews and joint planning independently, and identify and scope expansion in partnership with Sales.

 - Act as the voice of the partner internally, influencing roadmap, GTM strategy, and the tools we build.

 - Track adoption, usage, health and expansion to drive outcomes. Travel to partner sites roughly 3–5 times per quarter.

 - Operate AI-first by default, and build tools, agents, and workflows that eliminate recurring work for you and the team. Your impact is measured by the leverage you create, not only the partner you serve.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You have personally owned a strategic partner or customer relationship. Not supported one. You can describe what you decided, what you were accountable for, and what happened when it went badly.

 - Meaningful scale. Accounts or partner books at roughly $500K+ ARR each, or a partner relationship with comparable revenue attached. We want people who have handled real business-value partnerships at a strategic level.

 - Significant experience in technical, customer-facing roles at API-driven, developer-first, cloud, infrastructure, or AI companies. For most people that's roughly 7+ years, but we care more about the shape of your experience than the number.

 - Understanding of partner ecosystems and channel business models — resale, referral, integrations, marketplace, co-marketing, co-selling — and multi-party commercial dynamics.

 - Hands-on experience running demos, POCs, or technical workshops with enterprise partners or customers. Leading them, not attending them.

 - A track record of identifying and landing expansion in complex partner or enterprise relationships — opportunities you found, not ones handed to you.

 - Fluency discussing APIs, integrations, and developer workflows, and troubleshooting L1-style issues.

 - Experience engaging both technical stakeholders and executive buyers.

 - Exceptional communication and influence — concise and structured, across technical and business audiences.

 - Something you've built — a tool, agent, script, or workflow — that permanently eliminated recurring work. In your application, tell us what it was, what it replaced, and what it's still doing today.

 - An AI-native operating model: specific workflows that structurally depend on AI, and a clear account of how you'd rebuild them if those tools disappeared tomorrow.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Direct experience with the AWS ecosystem — Marketplace, private offers, CPPO, APN programs, MAP or other funding mechanisms, or co-sell with AWS field teams. This is a strong plus, not a requirement. We'd rather have a proven partner owner who learns AWS than an AWS specialist who has never owned an outcome.

 - Experience with consumption-based commercial models and how technical adoption converts to revenue.

 - Background in machine learning, voice AI, cloud infrastructure, GenAI/GPU workloads, or developer-first technologies.

 - Experience building a partner function from scratch at a smaller company.

 - Working fluency with automation, scripting, or agent-building (Python, TypeScript, workflow tools, agent frameworks, or equivalent). You don't need to be a software engineer — just dangerous enough to ship working systems.

This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

Deepgram is expanding into EMEA, and we're seeking a GM, Sales to own the region — building and leading the Enterprise and commercial segments of our Account Executive team, establishing Deepgram's European home in London, and driving growth across the region. We would like you to be in office 3-5 Days a week because of this!

This role is both strategic and hands-on. You'll work with sales leadership to continue optimizing the systems, playbooks, and culture that scale ARR growth, while developing a high-performing team that converts opportunities into long-lasting customers. A core part of your mission is building Deepgram's next generation of sales talent through world-class training, coaching, and structured career development.

You'll also be more than a revenue leader. As our senior-most voice in EMEA, you'll bring what you learn in the field back into the company and shape what we build — regional product-market fit, roadmap priorities, and the technical requirements European enterprises hold us to.

You'll partner closely with Marketing, Sales Leadership, RevOps, Customer Success, and Product to align pipeline strategy and leverage modern AI tools to boost productivity, personalization, and team efficiency. Equal parts operator, coach, and builder, you'll combine data-driven rigor with creativity to shape how Deepgram grows its customer base and its sales talent.

What You'll Do

  • Scale the Region: Own the EMEA P&L. Build and execute a strategic roadmap to drive hyper-growth in ARR, from initial land to enterprise-wide expansion.

  • Launch London: Stand up Deepgram's London office as our EMEA hub — and treat it as a commercial asset, not just real estate. It will host customer and developer events, executive briefings, partner sessions, and the team you build. We expect you to be operating out of this London office 3-5 days a week!

  • "Challenge & Lead": Recruit and mentor a high-performance team of Account Executives and one Sales Director. Manage Customer Success, Marketing, and Forward Deployed Engineers in a dotted-line structure. You will instill a culture of "Challenger" selling — teaching AEs how to disrupt legacy incumbents and lead with technical ROI.

  • Shape the Product: Act as the voice of EMEA inside Deepgram. Translate field signal — deal losses, evaluation criteria, data residency and compliance requirements, language and accent coverage — into specific, prioritized input that changes what we build and when.

  • Build the Ecosystem: Identify and sign strategic regional partners, GSIs, and local resellers to act as a force multiplier for Deepgram's direct sales efforts.

  • Operational Excellence: Implement rigorous forecasting, pipeline hygiene, and territory management across multiple countries, languages, and buying cultures. You will bridge the gap between London and our US HQ.

  • C-Suite Influence: Act as the primary executive sponsor for major regional accounts, navigating complex procurement cycles and technical AI evaluations.

You'll Love This Role If You

  • Thrive on building and scaling high-performing teams that consistently beat targets.

  • Want to build something from the ground up — including the office, the team, and the regional playbook.

  • Value working with tenured, high-caliber leaders who prioritize clarity, accountability, collaboration, and execution.

  • Enjoy blending data-driven sales operations with creative, human-centered leadership.

  • Are energized by developing AEs and building a culture of growth and continuous learning.

  • Believe in the power of AI to transform productivity, and are eager to harness cutting-edge tools to optimize performance.

  • Are passionate about Deepgram's mission to redefine what's possible with speech technology.

It's Important to Us That You Have

  • Experience: 12+ years in B2B SaaS sales, with 5+ years in a senior leadership role (Director/VP) covering EMEA — including the UK and at least one of DACH, the Nordics, France, or Southern Europe.

  • The "Deepgram DNA": A deep fascination with AI, LLMs, and API-first products. You should be comfortable discussing technical architecture as easily as you discuss revenue targets.

  • Product Influence: You've done more than sell — you've changed what your company built. You can point to specific roadmap decisions, features, or product bets that happened because of how you brought the market back to Product and Engineering.

  • Proven Growth: A track record of scaling a regional business from early traction to high-scale maturity ($10M+ ARR growth experience preferred).

  • Partnership Prowess: Demonstrable experience building channel programs that significantly contribute to the total revenue mix.

  • High ASP Focus: Expertise in value-based selling to increase Average Selling Price and win rates in a competitive technical landscape.

  • Operational Rigor: Deep familiarity with modern sales stacks (Salesforce, Gong, Clari, etc.) and a commitment to data-driven decision-making.

  • Education: Bachelor's degree required; MBA or technical degree is a plus.

It Would Be Great If You Had

  • Experience opening a new office or first in-region presence for a US-headquartered company.

  • Experience leading AE organizations at a high-growth, Series B+ startup or scaling tech company.

  • Background selling developer tools, infrastructure, or AI/ML technologies.

  • Fluency in navigating EU data protection and AI regulation as a commercial topic, not just a legal one.

  • Expertise in building talent development programs or performance coaching frameworks.

  • Comfort operating in dynamic, fast-moving environments with evolving goals and systems.

Backed by prominent investors including Atlantic Vantage Point (AVP), Y Combinator, Madrona, Tiger Global, Wing VC and NVIDIA, Deepgram has raised over $85 million in total funding. If you're looking to work on cutting-edge technology and make a significant impact in the AI industry, we'd love to hear from you!

Deepgram is an equal opportunity employer. We want all voices and perspectives represented in our workforce. We are a curious bunch focused on collaboration and doing the right thing. We put our customers first, grow together and move quickly. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, pregnancy, parental status, genetic information, political affiliation, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate.

jobs.title: Software Test Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity

Deepgram is looking for a Software Test Engineer to design, build, and maintain automated test frameworks and exploratory test suites across our products, models, APIs, and data platforms. You enjoy breaking systems, probing edge cases, testing real-world and adversarial inputs, and automating repeatable validation so regressions are caught quickly.

You translate product requirements and model metrics into automated regression tests, evaluation pipelines, data-quality gates, load tests, and release criteria. You partner with QA, Research, Product, Data, and Engineering to plan testing, execute human and automated evaluations, support user acceptance testing, and communicate risks clearly.

When you find an issue, you provide precise reproduction steps, inputs, parameters, expected and actual results, and supporting data. What gets you excited? Building scalable automation that gives Deepgram confidence that its products, models, and data workflows work reliably for customers.

What You'll Do

  • Define and execute well-designed test plans across Deepgram's products, APIs, SDKs, model-powered features, and data platforms, ensuring production software is robust, reliable, and performs well.

  • Design, build, and maintain automated test suites and frameworks for functional, integration, end-to-end, regression, API, browser, and service-level testing across batch and streaming workflows.

  • Translate product requirements and customer acceptance criteria into clear test strategies, repeatable test cases, and enforceable release gates.

  • Build and maintain representative, customer-focused, and adversarial test datasets, fixtures, and test environments that exercise real-world inputs, edge cases, failure modes, and system limits.

  • Validate model-powered behavior—including speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and other AI features—using appropriate metrics, expected outputs, human review, and regression coverage, while partnering with Research and model-evaluation specialists as needed.

  • Build testing infrastructure, including test harnesses, reusable scripts, test-data tooling, result-aggregation pipelines, dashboards, and visualizations that make quality signals easy to understand and act on.

  • Integrate automated tests, quality checks, canaries, and release validation into CI/CD so regressions are detected continuously rather than through manual testing alone.

  • Partner with Engineering, Product, Research, Data, Infrastructure, and DevOps to understand system behavior, dependencies, variations, performance limits, and deployment risks, and to establish appropriate test coverage.

  • Test data ingestion, processing, annotation, and quality-control workflows, validating data integrity, completeness, representativeness, deduplication, leakage, and downstream readiness.

  • Execute staging and production validation, load and reliability testing, cross-browser and customer-workflow testing, and user acceptance testing in partnership with internal stakeholders and customer QA teams.

  • Maintain and improve the test-case repository, automation coverage, test documentation, and release-readiness reporting so teams have a clear view of what was tested, what passed, and what remains risky.

  • Write precise, actionable bug reports with reproducible steps, inputs, parameters, expected and actual results, logs or artifacts, and clear severity; participate in triage and escalate issues when necessary.

  • Help raise the bar through code reviews, test-design reviews, technical discussions, and strong engineering, automation, and QA practices.

What We're Looking For

  • BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, AI, Applied Math, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • 5+ years of professional software or QA engineering experience, with a track record of shipping test infrastructure or evaluation systems (senior candidates with significantly deeper experience welcome).

  • Solid backend/scripting experience in a language such as Python, Rust, Go, or similar.

  • Experience designing and building automated test pipelines, evaluation frameworks, or data-processing systems.

  • Strong analytical skills and comfort reasoning about metrics, thresholds, and statistical variation in results — able to distinguish real regressions from noise.

  • Ability to take charge of ambiguous technical challenges and communicate effectively across research, engineering, and product teams.

Nice to Have / Ways to Stand Out

  • Hands-on experience testing or evaluating modern AI systems such as LLMs, RAG pipelines, agents, or multimodal models, including analyzing model behavior and failure modes.

  • Experience with voice, audio, speech recognition, or real-time systems, and familiarity with metrics such as WER, MOS, latency, and time-to-first-byte.

  • Experience building or improving test, evaluation, benchmarking, or ML infrastructure used by multiple teams or external users.

  • A strong appreciation for test and evaluation quality, including correctness, reproducibility, determinism, and consistency across environments.

  • Experience building test tooling for React Native, mobile applications, or other cross-platform environments that extends validation beyond the desktop.

  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, containers, ephemeral test environments, CI/CD systems, and monitoring tools such as Grafana, canaries, and anomaly detection.

  • Experience serving as a technical bridge across teams or platforms—including product, QA, evaluation, training, inference, data, or agent frameworks—with the communication skills to build alignment and influence decisions.

  • Prior involvement in open-source projects through contributions, reviews, maintenance, or community engagement.

  • Experience with voice, audio, speech recognition, or real-time systems, and familiarity with metrics like WER, MOS, or latency/TTFB.

  • Prior involvement in open-source projects, through contributions, reviews, maintenance, or community engagement.

  • Experience acting as a technical bridge across teams or platforms (evaluation, training, inference, agent frameworks), combining architectural understanding with clear communication and influence.

  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, containerized/ephemeral environments, and monitoring tooling (e.g. Grafana, canaries, anomaly detection).

THE OPPORTUNITY

Deepgram is looking for a Software Test Engineer to design, build, and maintain automated test frameworks and exploratory test suites across our products, models, APIs, and data platforms. You enjoy breaking systems, probing edge cases, testing real-world and adversarial inputs, and automating repeatable validation so regressions are caught quickly. 

You translate product requirements and model metrics into automated regression tests, evaluation pipelines, data-quality gates, load tests, and release criteria. You partner with QA, Research, Product, Data, and Engineering to plan testing, execute human and automated evaluations, support user acceptance testing, and communicate risks clearly.
